papers.abstract: Quantized charge pumping in quantum Hall systems is a bulk topological property, typically manifesting on gapless boundaries as spectral flow through chiral edge modes upon flux insertion. When the boundary is anomaly-free, it can be symmetrically gapped by symmetric mass generation (SMG) interactions. However, the effects on quantized charge pumping at an interacting gapped boundary are unclear. We address this using density-matrix renormalization group simulations of a four-leg ladder quasi-(2+1)d realization of the (1+1)d 3-4-5-0 lattice chiral fermion model with six-fermion interactions at one edge. We find gapless modes near the interacting edge for both weak and strong couplings, but the edge can be in a fully gapped SMG phase at intermediate coupling. We also identify spontaneous breaking of the model's $\mathbb{Z}_2$ symmetry above a critical interaction strength. Across all three boundary phases, we find quantized charge pumping with the same pumped charge per flux quantum. The spatial distribution of the pumped charge varies between phases. Besides charge pumping, we study how a single injected fermion propagates under open boundary conditions. In the SMG phase, an interaction-induced flavor-mixing current develops at the endpoints of the gapped edge, which is absent in the weak- and strong-coupling limits. This current reveals a charge-redistribution mechanism unique to the SMG phase. Additionally, we propose an analogy between charge pumping in this model and a topological leptogenesis scenario in the (3+1)d Standard Model. The anomaly-free chiral U(1) symmetries of the 3-4-5-0 model play a role analogous to the baryon-minus-lepton symmetry of the Standard Model. In both settings, charge pumping can be associated with a continuous deformation along a classically defined but quantum-anomalous direction, while a discrete subgroup remains an exact quantum symmetry.
papers.authors: Runze Chi, Meng Zeng, Tao Xiang, Yi-Zhuang You, Bertrand I. Halperin, Juven Wang

papers.title: An Egorov-type Theorem for Analytic Wick Observables in Quantum Field Theory
papers.abstract: We provide an exact Egorov-type formula, given by a convergent expansion in the semi-classical parameter $\varepsilon > 0$, for the propagation of a certain class of analytic Wick observables with super-exponentially decaying coefficients, under the action of a time-dependent quadratic Hamiltonian. This work generalizes a result established by S. Breteaux for polynomial symbols, and includes the spatially cutoff $P(\varphi)_2$ model, as well as a variant of the H\"oegh-Krohn model.
papers.authors: Julien Malartre

papers.title: Maximum-Entropy Ensemble of Quantum Subsystems with a Fixed Average State
papers.abstract: The reduced density matrices of Haar-random bipartite states form a fixed-trace version of the Wishart ensemble of random matrices, with an asymptotic eigenvalue density given by the Marchenko-Pastur (MP) law. We establish a similar universal form for the maximum-entropy distribution of mixed states subject to a fixed ensemble average, arguing that its eigenvalue density converges asymptotically to that of the correlated Wishart ensemble (CWE). The density is thus obtained by a free multiplicative convolution formula, which we apply to the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM) with a thermal average state to derive a high-temperature leading-order correction to the MP law. We then consider measurement by a random POVM on the purification of the mixed reference state. We show that the resulting mixed-state ensemble is asymptotically equivalent to the CWE, and provide confirming numerical evidence. We return to the TFIM example to compute the entanglement of the system with the ancilla after measurement, and give finite-temperature Page curves for the average entanglement entropies.
papers.authors: Charlie Shakeshaft, Christopher David White, Harry J. D. Miller

papers.title: Gravitational baryogenesis in Gauss-Bonnet braneworld cosmology
papers.abstract: The present study investigates the feasibility of gravitational baryogenesis in a Gauss-Bonnet (GB) modified Randall-Sundrum (RS) type II braneworld cosmology. The modified expansion rate of the Universe in this scenario evolves through three distinct expansion regimes, the GB regime at early times where the expansion rate $H \sim \rho^{1/3}$ falls more slowly than the standard expansion law $H\sim \rho^{1/2}$ of GR, then the RS type era with an enhanced expansion $H \sim \rho$, before finally reducing to the standard expansion law in the low energy limit. Gravitational baryogenesis depends on $\dot{R}$ and requires $\dot{R} <0$. This condition is satisfied for the GB and GR regimes. However, $\dot{R}>0$ for the RS regime and successful baryogenesis requires either that the decoupling temperature occurs during the GB regime or that the Universe makes a direct transition from the GB regime to the GR regime. The GB baryon asymmetry $\eta(T)$ is proportional to $\mu (1+w)(1-w)(1+1/\beta)$, where $\mu$ is the energy scale $\mu \equiv 1/l$ associated with the bulk curvature scale $l$, $\beta \equiv 4 \alpha \mu^{2}$, where $\alpha$ is the GB coupling, and $w$ is the equation of state parameter $p=w \rho$. Studies of inflation in GB-braneworld cosmology place constraints on the allowed ranges of the parameters $\mu$ and $\beta$. Guided by these, the asymmetry has been calculated for ranges of $(\mu, \beta, w)$ and it is found that the observed values can be obtained for a value of $\beta$ within the range $(10^{-2} - 10^{-3})$ for $\mu =10^{12}$ GeV, and within the range $(10^{-1}- 10^{-2})$ for $\mu =10^{13}$ GeV. All values of $\eta$ for $\mu=10^{14}$ are too high. The parameter ranges for the decoupling temperatures required to produce the observed asymmetry have also been established.
papers.authors: Ian B Whittingham

papers.title: The 't Hooft model on (A)dS$_2$
papers.abstract: We solve large-$N$ two-dimensional QCD with fundamental quarks---the 't Hooft model---on rigid AdS$_2$ and dS$_2$. Their isometries preserve the null gauge $A_-=0$ and in affine coordinates the curvature enters the light-front Hamiltonian only through the special-conformal generator of the null line. The $SL(2,\mathbb{R)}$ Casimir then results in an exact meson equation: 't Hooft's equation plus a Legendre operator whose sign is determined by the curvature. On AdS$_2$ it is related to equations proposed in the context of folded/segmented strings and light-front holography. The pion is massless in the chiral limit and obeys a Gell-Mann--Oakes--Renner relation that fixes the chiral condensate, the dimensions cross over from Regge to logarithmic growth once the flux tube exceeds the curvature radius, and the flat-space integrable structure survives. We also solve the problem of a quark interacting with an antiquark placed at the boundary: beyond a critical coupling the string pulls it back to the boundary, resulting in a scattering phase. On dS$_2$ and due to the expansion of space, the mesons are unstable resonances even at $N=\infty$ and eventually dissociate. Their widths are given by Boltzmann factors at the de Sitter temperature.
papers.authors: Panos Betzios

papers.title: Covariant Wigner function and spin polarization of the Rarita-Schwinger field
papers.abstract: We study the covariant Wigner function for the spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field and its relation to the spin density matrix and the mean spin polarization vector. We obtain a formula relating the covariant Wigner function to the mean spin vector for a weakly interacting field. We then calculate the mean spin vector induced by thermal vorticity, thermal shear, and spin potential at local thermal equilibrium in the Belinfante, canonical and GLW pseudo-gauges. The resulting formula can be used to predict the spin polarization of spin-$3/2$ hadrons, such as the $\Omega^-$, in heavy-ion collisions. Differences in the thermal-shear induced polarization in the canonical and Belinfante pseudo-gauges make it possible to use local spin polarization measurements of the $\Omega^-$ to discriminate between the two pseudo-gauges. Lastly, we obtain the axial vortical effect conductivity for the free massive spin-$3/2$ Rarita-Schwinger field.
papers.authors: Matteo Buzzegoli, Aleksandar Gecic, Rajeev Singh

papers.title: Diagnostic-dependent lasting Mpemba effect in a parametrically driven oscillator
papers.abstract: Agreement on the initial order does not ensure agreement on the late-time behavior in the quantum Mpemba effect. For a pair of centered Gaussian preparations of a detuned parametric oscillator below threshold, three diagnostics initially give the same order. At late times, the trace distance shows a lasting Mpemba reversal, the relative entropy recovers the initial order, and the Hilbert-Schmidt distances cross at arbitrarily late times. An asymptotic analysis establishes these behaviors and their stability under small changes of the initial covariances and the quadratic generator. Equal decay rates keep an energy mode and a pair of squeezing modes comparable at late times. This structure holds for stable single-mode quadratic generators with linear damping in the elliptic regime. The diagnostics weight the resulting purity and squeezing deviations differently; near a pure stationary state, the relative entropy is particularly sensitive to purity deviations. Weak perturbations can split these rates and select a dominant branch. For the same pair, number dephasing restores the initial order in all three diagnostics, possibly only after the signal falls below measurement resolution. A Kerr perturbation selecting the squeezing pair instead produces a common lasting reversal.
papers.authors: Shu He

papers.title: Simplifying 2-Bundle Descriptions of Invariants and Local Dynamics
papers.abstract: A string couples to a 2-form gauge potential whose local descriptions need not fit together as a single global form. Principal 2-bundles provide a geometric description of this gluing. However, we recover surface amplitudes and quantum partition functions, as well as local classical field dynamics, without the 2-bundle formalism. For surface amplitudes, differential characters preserve curvature and flat phases. Ordinary fake-flat crossed-module connections with a fixed flat quotient and a reference lift lead to abelian differential cocycles with local coefficients. In three-dimensional finite gauge theories with cohomological actions, Fourier transformation evaluates the 2-form field sum and gives a sum of ordinary finite-group gauge partition functions. A four-dimensional quadratic example gives a signature response that admits direct cochain evaluation although replacement by an ordinary finite-group gauge theory fails. Established bundle, operator, and module descriptions provide further comparisons for topological and index invariants and twisted-sheaf moduli. For finite-dimensional smoothly separable central crossed modules, an invertible local substitution removes a pure gauge 1-form from invariant classical actions for any adjustment, leaving an ordinary quotient connection and two tensor fields. One of these tensor fields can be separated globally from the remaining lift data after fixing the quotient connection and choosing a smooth bundle splitting. For compact or semisimple quotients, an equivariant splitting makes this separation compatible with the full gauge symmetry without changing the adjustment.
papers.authors: Ferreira Bastien

papers.title: Fast and accurate rare-event simulation by Markov chain Monte Carlo for general quantum codes
papers.abstract: The splitting method estimates logical error rates of quantum error-correcting codes deep in the rare-event regime, where direct Monte Carlo sampling is prohibitively expensive. It relies on a Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampler of faulty configurations, usually driven by one-bit-flip proposals. However, one-bit flips have been reported to be trapped on some codes, which biases the estimate. To address this issue, we propose a new kernel that combines locally balanced one-bit-flip proposals with a cluster-exchange move. We benchmark both kernels and direct Monte Carlo on twelve codes under code-capacity bit-flip noise in two ways, by comparing the mean fault weight with an MCMC-independent reference and by measuring the computation time to reach a fixed accuracy. In the first, our kernel agrees with the reference on every code, including those where one-bit flips are trapped. In the second, it is faster than one-bit flips wherever they are trapped, by orders of magnitude on some codes. Furthermore, at the lowest error rate, it is faster than direct Monte Carlo on every code, by more than four orders of magnitude on some.
papers.authors: Junichi Haruna, Kotaro Murakami

papers.title: Trial-space co-design for quantum simulation on noisy hardware
papers.abstract: Quantum simulations on noisy hardware are often designed as if the machine were ideal, with device limitations considered only after the basis and measurement plan have been chosen. We instead use information about the physical problem and the device at an earlier stage, to decide which states and evolution times should form a compact simulation basis. Because the target problem remains unchanged, the method adapts only the representation used to solve it. Tests on many-body and molecular models show that this approach can reveal useful directions that ordinary time evolution misses, while also exposing an important limitation: some of these directions can become too similar to estimate reliably. Realistic device data further show that hardware response can change the preferred states and evolution times before execution. Across seven acquisition days, a four-qubit experiment shows a median 54\% reduction in projected-energy error from problem-informed time choices relative to uniform sampling under matched hardware conditions. These results provide a proof of principle for simulation-basis design as a practical interface between quantum algorithms and the hardware that executes them.
papers.authors: Bo Peng, Vibin Abraham, Himadri Pathak

papers.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
papers.abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.
papers.authors: Dean Wang

papers.title: Fermions Scattering Off Non-Abelian Rotors
papers.abstract: We study the dynamics of $d=1+1$ chiral fermions interacting with a rotor impurity. The rotors are non-Abelian, taking values in either an $SU(N)$ group manifold, or an $SU(N)/SO(N)$ coset. At low energies, the fermions pass through the impurity, seemingly unimpeded, but trailing a topological line that is necessary for current conservation. In certain cases, these topological lines exhibit non-Abelian fusion and braiding. This can be viewed as a toy model that captures aspects of s-wave monopole-fermion scattering in $d=3+1$ dimensions.
papers.authors: George Koundouros, David Tong

papers.title: Onsager Algebras and Lattice Fermions
papers.abstract: We study the exact Onsager algebra of free lattice fermions in staggered, Wilson, and overlap incarnations, working in both Hamiltonian and Euclidean formulations in four spacetime dimensions. In each case, we show that the exact lattice algebra emanates the full chiral symmetry of the low-energy theory: if there are $N$ massless Dirac fermions in the continuum, the Onsager algebra reduces to a $U(2N)$ chiral symmetry. The details of which generators are quantised or ultra-local differ between formulations. There is also a trade-off between the locality of generators and the maximum compact subgroup of the Onsager algebra.
papers.authors: Ioanna Kourkoulou, David Tong

papers.title: Monodromy Defects of 3D Wilson-Fisher Criticality on the Fuzzy Sphere
papers.abstract: Monodromy line defects arise as boundaries of topological symmetry surfaces, providing a natural route to conformal defects with implications in condensed matter, gauge theories and quantum information. However, their interacting dynamics remains difficult to characterize non-perturbatively. Here we realize monodromy boundary conditions in the fuzzy-sphere regularization by threading a symmetry-selective Aharonov-Bohm flux through the two poles of the sphere. We apply this construction to the $Z_2$ twist of the 3D Ising conformal field theory (CFT), the $\pi$-twist of the 3D O(2) CFT, and three inequivalent monodromies of O(3) (centre twist, z-axis $\pi$-twist and reflection). For each defect we extract the low-lying defect spectrum together with bulk-to-defect and defect-defect operator product expansion coefficients, which characterize the operators living on the defect line, their mutual interactions, and how they couple to the critical bulk. Among the resolved low-lying defect primaries we find no relevant scalar perturbation preserving all symmetries of the corresponding defect; the relevant deformations identified break at least one preserved symmetry, providing evidence that these monodromy defects are stable against symmetry-preserving relevant perturbations. For the partial twists of O(3), we derive the flow of the symmetry-preserving untwisted zero-mode mass generated by the bulk interaction. Its weak-coupling runaway near four dimensions motivates a careful distinction between the microscopic absence of pinning, the free reference background, and a possible infrared defect fixed point in three dimensions. These results establish a systematic set of non-perturbative conformal data for monodromy defects beyond the Ising twist, turning the symmetry flux into a tunable knob of the fuzzy-sphere regularization for exploring the response of critical matter to distinct defects.
papers.authors: Yin Tang, W. Zhu

papers.title: Finding CFTs from spatial positivity of partition functions
papers.abstract: We discuss a positivity property for partition functions that generalizes modular invariance and which is here conjectured to hold for general 2D CFTs. We show its relation to positivity properties of R\'enyi entropies and its meaning in terms of topological defect lines. We apply the conjecture to find consistent local unitary CFT models which are not necessarily modular invariant.
papers.authors: L\'eo Buisine, Horacio Casini, Leandro Martinek

papers.title: Mechanical angular momentum loss at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ from static and radiative gravitons
papers.abstract: We determine the loss of mechanical angular momentum $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$ of two gravitationally scattering bodies at $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ using worldline quantum field theory (WQFT). The gravitational memory effect, a phenomenon of the early- and late-time behaviour of the gravitational field, leads to static contributions to $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$. We illuminate how these arise: the linear memory contributes through so-called static correlators, while the nonlinear memory vanishes at this order due to symmetry considerations. The computation of the remaining, dynamical part resembles that of the $\mathcal{O}(G^4)$ impulse. We generate its integrand using a reformulation of the WQFT Feynman rules that conserves four-momentum at every vertex and plainly exhibits the classical loops. The three-loop integrals are reduced to master integrals, whose differential equations and boundary matching in the post-Newtonian limit we describe in some detail. In contrast to conservative effects at this order, only polylogarithms appear. While individual contributions to the dynamical part are divergent, these cancel in $L^{\mu}_{\rm loss}$. The quadratic-in-radiation part of our result reproduces earlier results, while the complete result agrees with existing post-Newtonian results.
papers.authors: Lara Bohnenblust, Carl Jordan Eriksen, Gustav Uhre Jakobsen, Kathrin Stoldt, Andrii Yanovets

papers.title: Flux-Based Time Bounds for Harmonically Degenerate Quantum Systems
papers.abstract: We study transfer-time estimates for finite-dimensional bilinear quantum control systems driven by an unbounded scalar control, in both the state-to-state setting (complex projective space) and the unitary synthesis setting (special unitary group). Lower bounds are recalled and refined via spectral and chordal methods. The main contribution is constructive upper bounds: we associate with the system a coupling graph whose edges correspond to non-resonant drift couplings, and construct transfer protocols along spanning trees. In contrast with earlier results requiring full rational independence of the spectrum of the control operator, our estimates allow rational resonances; they incorporate, via explicit correction factors derived from the arithmetic of the spectral gaps, the efficiency of the averaging procedure and of the phase adjustments. As an application, we consider finite-dimensional truncations of the planar quantum rotator under a dipolar electric field, and show that the transfer time between any two modes tends to zero as the truncation dimension grows.
papers.authors: Thomas Chambrion (IRMA,UNISTRA)

papers.title: Scalar fields in the background of a linear Vaidya spacetime
papers.abstract: We study, in a semiclassical, quasi-stationary approximation, the entanglement properties of massless scalar fields near the event horizon of a dynamical black hole modeled by an ingoing Vaidya metric with a linearly decaying mass. In the near-horizon limit, the geometry becomes conformally equivalent to an eternal black hole, allowing the use of modular theory to analyze vacuum entanglement. We first study the modifications to the entanglement across the bifurcation surface of such a black hole from that of an eternal one. The conformal factor accounting for the evaporation modifies the Bogoliubov transformation between global modes and modes across the bifurcate Killing horizon of the black hole, inducing a phase in the thermofield-double-like structure of the global vacuum. This phase change of the vacuum state is a consequence of the adiabatic shift of the horizon. A quantitative measure of the entanglement change due to the phase is obtained through the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) inequality. We compare the CHSH inequalities in the vacuum states for the static and the linear Vaidya black holes and find that the CHSH correlation quantity for the latter is decreased by a factor dependent on the evaporation rate. Next, we discuss the analysis of the linear Vaidya black hole formed from gravitational collapse. For this purpose we adapt an analysis by Wald for the case of the Schwarzschild black hole. The entangled global vacuum again has a thermofield double structure. However, we find, as expected, the near-horizon structure and state do not approach that of the eternal black hole. Rather, the thermal factor is modified by a factor incorporating the change in the black hole mass due to evaporation.
papers.authors: Arielle Schutz, Ratindranath Akhoury

papers.title: Jianmu-Q: Bridging Quantum Field Theory and Quantum Hardware with AI Agents
papers.abstract: Quantum computing offers a promising approach to non-perturbative simulations of quantum field theories, particularly for real-time dynamics and systems affected by the sign problem. Yet translating continuum field theories into quantum computations remains a challenging interdisciplinary task. Here we introduce \texttt{Jianmu-Q}, a multi-agent framework that transforms natural-language descriptions of quantum field theories into quantum simulation workflows. Specialized agents handle theoretical formulation, lattice discretization, qubit mapping, and circuit design, while physical consistency checks and independent numerical calculations provide validation throughout the workflow. We benchmark the framework on three field theories of increasing complexity: the $(1+1)$-dimensional Nambu--Jona-Lasinio and Schwinger models, and a $(2+1)$-dimensional $\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory. Across these systems, noiseless quantum-circuit simulations converge toward independent exact-diagonalization and tensor-network results, while selected circuits are executed on IBM quantum hardware, demonstrating an end-to-end, validation-guided approach to quantum simulation of field theories.
papers.authors: Xiaolin Wang, Xingyu Guo, Jinyang Li, Tianyin Li, Enke Wang, Lingxiao Wang, Hongxi Xing

papers.title: Strong subadditivity of topological entropy on the torus: R\'enyi order and non-Abelian structure
papers.abstract: We classify universal strong subadditivity of the canonical topological entropy on an unpunctured torus across all pure logical states and admissible region pairs, for finite unitary modular tensor categories and finite positive R\'enyi orders. Below order one, universal validity is equivalent to Abelian, or pointed, anyon structure. At the von Neumann order it holds for every category. In nonpointed categories, shared topological flux and unequal occupied quantum dimensions curve the multi-annulus response, producing violations at every finite positive order other than one. Every category of rank greater than one admits a single state and region pair that violate the inequality for all finite orders at least two. The remaining pointed orders strictly between one and two are governed by an exact equal-order modular Fourier criterion. On the lattice, a specified quantum-double reference ground state for each finite non-Abelian group realizes the nonpointed violations directly in ordinary physical-edge entropies on a common refinement. Applying the same diagonal filter to every physical edge gives a controlled deformation of this reference state. For each fixed group, a common size-independent small parameter interval supports a uniform R\'enyi-two deficit bound and a uniformly gapped local parent for all cost profiles bounded between zero and one, within the stated lattice family. Nonconstant profiles change regional entanglement spectra near the fixed point at every fixed finite volume in the specified strip geometry. The deficit converges to its strictly negative fixed-point value in the controlled joint limit of system size and interface separation.
papers.authors: Yi Liang

papers.title: Shot- and Noise-Aware Pauli Correlation Encoding for Max-Cut Experiments on IBM Heron Quantum Processor
papers.abstract: Pauli correlation encoding (PCE) encodes $m$ binary variables in the signs of $k$-body Pauli correlators of $n=O(m^{1/k})$ qubits, and trains a parameterized circuit on a relaxed loss of sharpness $\alpha$. The strongest published schedules sharpen this loss aggressively and are benchmarked with exact expectation values, whereas a quantum computer estimates correlators from a finite number of shots. We show that the sharpness is a hidden shot budget. Since the expected sign of a correlator estimated from $S$ shots, $\mathrm{erf}(c\sqrt{S/2})$, agrees with $\tanh(0.851\sqrt{S}\,c)$ to within $0.019$, the edge term of the relaxed loss at $\alpha=0.851\sqrt{S}$ approximately equals, up to a constant, minus twice the cut expected from decoding $S$ shots. This explains why schedules tuned with exact expectation values lose their advantage at realistic budgets, and yields a shot-aware schedule whose final sharpness is set by the shot budget. On five G-set graphs with $800$ variables on $13$ qubits, this schedule outperforms every published schedule at its target budget in all $150$ paired comparisons of the decoded circuit output, owing to the sharpness at $1.6\times10^4$ shots and mostly to switching off the regularization at $10^3$; after a classical bit-swap search, it remains the best on average at $1.6\times10^4$ shots. Device noise damps the correlators by a factor $s$, which amounts to a smaller shot budget $s^2S$. On the IBM Heron processor ibm_fez, an all-to-all ansatz of the type used for the best published G-set results compiles to $835$ CZ gates and decodes to a random cut, while our $96$-CZ hardware-native circuit, trained in simulation and sharpened to $\alpha\simeq0.65\,s\sqrt{S}$, retains up to $0.919$ of the best-known cut. For new circuits, a damping and an offset calibrated on other circuits of the same graph predicted the decoded cuts at $10^3$ shots to within $0.002$.
papers.authors: Achraf Boussahi

papers.title: Under what conditions can coupling disorder render qubit dynamics CP-divisible in a finite spin bath?
papers.abstract: We investigate whether unresolved quasi-static Gaussian disorder in system--bath coupling can make finite spin-bath dynamics CP-divisible. The coupling varies between shots but is fixed within each, yielding a disorder-averaged tomographic map. For a single-spin Ising $ZZ$ bath with a fixed initial state, disorder can induce a polarization-dependent transition to CP-divisibility. A bath fully polarized along the longitudinal direction ($|m_z|=1$) yields CP-divisible dynamics irrespective of disorder, whereas zero longitudinal polarization or Haar-sampled bath states fluctuating independently of the coupling between shots preserve CP-indivisibility at any finite disorder strength for nonzero mean coupling. We extend this analytically to inhomogeneous Ising baths of any finite size $N$. For factorized bath preparations, one spin with zero longitudinal polarization and nonzero mean coupling suffices to retain CP-indivisibility at finite disorder. Strong disorder can render partially polarized baths CP-divisible. For homogeneous baths, the critical disorder ratio is independent of $N$. When bath states fluctuate physically between shots, independent Haar sampling preserves CP-indivisibility for finite $N$ if any mean coupling is nonzero. For a single-spin anisotropic Heisenberg bath, any nonzero transverse exchange preserves trace-distance backflow at finite disorder for every fixed preparation, provided the mean coupling is nonzero. Exact diagonalization up to $N=12$ shows trace-distance revivals for a fully polarized bath, in Haar averages over fixed product bath states, and for fluctuating bath states. Transverse exchange and physical bath-state fluctuations with zero average longitudinal polarization preserve CP-indivisibility at finite disorder. Yet increasing disorder can make trace-distance revivals experimentally unresolvable, making the dynamics appear Markovian.
papers.authors: Sayan Sengupta, Anish Sharma, George Biswas, Anindya Biswas

papers.title: Cosmic Colliders in Binary Blazars Probing Ultra-High-Energy Particle Physics
papers.abstract: While terrestrial colliders and fixed-target cosmic-ray interactions are bounded at center-of-mass (CM) energies $\sqrt{s} \lesssim \mathcal{O}(10^5)\,\text{GeV}$, we demonstrate that sub-parsec binary blazars form broad-band hadronic ``Cosmic Colliders'', overcoming this limitation. In the compressed overlap region of two nearly aligned jets ($\theta_{\rm mis} \sim 1^\circ - 5^\circ$), relativistic proton populations collide at CM energies reaching $\sqrt{s} \sim 10^{10}\,\text{GeV}$ -- six orders of magnitude above the Large Hadron Collider. Operating in an optically thin regime ($\tau_{pp} \ll 1$), the system performs a continuous CM energy scan, probing asymptotic QCD scaling, gluon saturation, and Froissart unitarity, while opening a possible high-sensitivity window into physics beyond the Standard Model. Secondary TeV-EeV neutrinos and GeV-TeV $\gamma$-rays fall within the reach of current and planned observatories such as LHAASO, CTAO, IceCube, and GRAND, establishing binary blazars as laboratories for physics at the ultimate energy limit.
papers.authors: Giorgio Galanti

papers.title: Geodesic steering for rapid dissipative entanglement distribution
papers.abstract: We describe an optimal-control strategy designed to accelerate the dissipative preparation of complex, highly entangled quantum many-body states. Analogous to optimal steering of isolated quantum systems, our scheme identifies control pulses that guide the evolution of open quantum systems along trajectories of instantaneous steady states while minimizing leakage resulting from non-adiabatic transitions. In many cases of interest, these control parameters can be derived analytically and without the need for computationally expensive numerical simulations of the full many-body master equation. We apply this technique for the preparation of bi- and multipartite entangled states in qubit systems coupled to a common photonic waveguide or a distributed squeezed reservoir. In both scenarios, our optimal-control strategy significantly outperforms the bare relaxation dynamics after a quench, reducing preparation times of near-maximally entangled states by orders of magnitude. This drastic speedup makes dissipative entanglement distribution protocols compatible with high-fidelity quantum information processing applications and illustrates more broadly the potential of leakage minimization for accelerating reservoir-engineering schemes.
papers.authors: Keshav Venkataraman, Pablo Martinez-Azcona, Marko Ljubotina, Adrian Parra-Rodriguez, Peter Rabl

papers.title: TheoPhysEval: Assessing AI agents at autonomous theoretical physics problem solving
papers.abstract: We present a suite of 50 unpublished research-level theoretical physics problems with verifiable answers. Without AI assistance, a typical problem in our collection could be solved by a world expert in about a day or less but would take considerably longer for experts in adjacent specialties. We test the ability of off-the-shelf AI agents to tackle these problems autonomously, without human hints. When given access to tools available in a realistic setting, including the ability to search the literature and write scripts for numerical and symbolic work, the best-performing agent, GPT-6-Astra harnessed in Codex, obtains the final answers with a near-perfect accuracy of 98% at an average cost under USD 3 per problem. On average, agents show only small changes in accuracy when denied web search and access to background research papers, suggesting significant memorization of the literature. These results suggest that state-of-the-art agents can accurately perform concrete calculations required across theoretical physics research. We comment on the broader implications of these findings and discuss possible explanations for the current lack of agent-led breakthroughs in theoretical physics despite their outstanding problem-solving abilities.
papers.authors: A. Ramesh Chandra, Aaghaz Mahajan, Ainesh Sanyal, Mianqi Wang, Shubhadeep Chakraborty, Sudip Chakraborty, Shailesh Chandrasekharan, Rama Govindarajan, Akshit Goyal, Jonathan J. Heckman, Yasir Iqbal, Divya Jaganathan, Saumav Kapoor, Andreas Karch, Pushkar Khandare, Sandeep Krishna, Anupam Kundu, Alok Laddha, Tongyan Lin, Swarnendu Maity, Nilmani Mathur, Shani Nadir Meynet, Alessandro Mininno, Abhijeet Mishra, Vidur Niranjan, Abhishodh Prakash, Pratik Rath, Durbar Roy, Debargha Sarkar, Srikanth Sastry, Gary Shiu, Aninda Sinha, Thomas Van Riet, Praneeth Netrapalli, Suvrat Raju

papers.title: Time-Frequency Continuous-Variable Quantum Teleportation with Single Photons
papers.abstract: Quantum teleportation, a key building block for quantum technologies, enables distant parties, Alice and Bob, to transfer an unknown quantum state using entanglement, local operations, and classical communication. In this work, we propose a quantum teleportation protocol for single-photon time-frequency continuous variables, where time is the time of arrival at a detector. We detail the operational requirements of the protocol, notably the nonlinear interactions needed for the photon-photon time-frequency entangling gate. By explicitly treating the detector position as the reference frame for time of arrival, we show that, even with ideal classical and quantum channels, the input-output fidelity is not unity unless the receiving party can correct the detector-position mismatch. This results in a trade-off between teleportation fidelity and the temporal bandwidth of the input photon wavepacket. The protocol itself can be used for remote detector synchronization. In particular, we show that time-frequency cat and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states provide an internal temporal ruler through fidelity revivals. We further derive the classical and best-copy fidelity thresholds for single-photon Gaussian wavepackets, finding that the relevant vacuum-equivalent shot noise is input-dependent, in contrast with quadrature-based continuous-variable quantum teleportation. Our proposal derives from a quantum theory of space-time events, whereafter we establish space as a reference for the time degree of freedom, thereby grounding our work in ongoing research on reference frames and superselection rules in quantum optics and quantum information. Beyond protocols harnessing time-frequency continuous variables of single photons, this work points toward remote synchronization in quantum communication architectures.
papers.authors: Mohamed Meguebel, Nadia Belabas, Nicolas Fabre

papers.title: Sample-Based Quantum Krylov Galerkin Solvers for Elliptic Partial Differential Equations on Curved Geometries with Hardware Validation
papers.abstract: Sample-based quantum solvers measure time-evolved Krylov states and solve the problem classically on the observed basis states. We develop this approach for the positive-definite linear systems of elliptic partial differential equations. A Galerkin solve on the sampled Fourier modes gives the solution. We derive energy-norm error bounds that connect the measured outcome law to the solution error, a sample complexity, and a support-completeness theorem. The theorem shows that time averaging recovers solution modes that are hidden from every selection based on the source. For curved cross sections we give a constructive procedure: conformal coordinates fix the matrix class, isometries of the cross section give postselection rules that keep every solution mode, and the Lie derivative of the metric bounds the error from geometric uncertainty. We apply the method to pulsatile flow in elliptic, lens-shaped, and curved ducts and to non-separable problems with up to 16 qubits. On 16 qubits the sampler reaches 0.2% error with 3% of the Fourier modes, while a selection from the source stalls at 13% error. At these sizes a classical residual-greedy selection is more accurate, but its cost grows with the full dimension, whereas the sampler and the reduced Galerkin solve scale with the number of sampled modes. On IonQ and IBM processors with six and eight qubits, the measured outcome laws follow a replacement-noise model with a common decay of about 0.6% per two-qubit gate, and a parity rule derived from the geometry detects noisy shots at the predicted rate.
papers.authors: Doyeol "David" Ahn (Center for Quantum Information Processing, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea, Singularity Quantum Inc., Villa Park, California, USA), Byeongyong Park (Center for Quantum Information Processing, University of Seoul, Dongdaemun-gu, Seoul, Republic of Korea)

papers.title: Gluons and Knots
papers.abstract: We argue that the scattering amplitude of a single minus helicity gluon with arbitrarily many positive helicity gluons is topological. The amplitude is constant in chambers of kinematic space, its resonances are located at walls and its factorization is determined by wall-crossing. Yangian invariance dictates the amplitude to be determined by a 2d null Wilson loop that can be lifted into a positive and transverse 3d link. By reinterpreting wall-crossing and the Weinberg soft theorem as skein relations and Reidemeister moves of the subknots, we construct a state-counting description consisting of adding the `corners' of their HOMFLY-PT polynomials. Beyond the classical limit, we argue that this provides a conjectured but precise connection to topological field and string theory. The new formula is rigorously derived via a Lean-formalized dependency graph (DAG) as detailed in a companion paper, laying out the precise assumptions including Reidemeister III invariance. It is further tested exhaustively, including novel `star' kinematics where the amplitude and state count are shown to become Catalan numbers, in agreement with knot theory literature.
papers.authors: Alfredo Guevara

papers.title: Almost-splitting of spacetimes under timelike sectional curvature bounds
papers.abstract: We establish an almost-splitting theorem for spacetimes under timelike sectional curvature bounds in the spirit of the celebrated Riemannian result due to Cheeger and Colding. More concretely, we show that if a globally hyperbolic spacetime with timelike sectional curvature bounded below by a nonpositive constant close to zero contains a long maximizing timelike segment, then causal diamonds along that segment are close in the Lorentzian Gromov--Hausdorff sense of Minguzzi--Suhr to those in a product metric spacetime. Our result can be interpreted as a quantitative analogue of the Lorentzian splitting theorem for spacetimes with nonnegative timelike sectional curvature by Beem--Ehrlich--Markvorsen--Galloway. In contrast to the Riemannian setting, the timelike sectional curvature bound cannot be replaced by Ricci-flatness, as the small mass limit of the Schwarzschild exterior geometry shows.
papers.authors: Nicola Gigli, Melanie Graf, Robert J. McCann, Argam Ohanyan, Eric Woolgar, Matteo Zanardini

papers.title: Extensively degenerate superradiant phase in a giant-atom quantum Rabi ring
papers.abstract: We show that an $N$-site quantum Rabi ring with matched giant-atom couplings has $2^N$ degenerate superradiant configurations as the atomic-to-cavity frequency ratio $\eta=\Delta/\omega$ tends to infinity. Each atom couples to two cavities separated by two lattice spacings, and the photon hopping carries a phase $\pi/2$. Matching the ratio of the two coupling strengths to the dimensionless photon hopping reduces the mean-field energy to a sum of single-site Rabi energies, with a common critical coupling for all momentum-pair sectors. The degeneracy survives quadratic quantum fluctuations despite a dispersive excitation spectrum. At large but finite $\eta$, second-order processes involving the local cubic anharmonicity generate a same-sublattice Ising coupling of order $\omega/\eta$, selecting ferro- and antiferro-superradiant configurations. This quantum order-by-disorder effect has no classical counterpart. Four-site calculations retaining all spin states quantitatively support the predicted energy coefficients. The separation between the induced coupling and the excitation gap allows a broad temperature interval with macroscopic photon occupation and short-range correlations between displacement signs.
papers.authors: Shu He, Li-Wei Duan

papers.title: No-Disturbance-without-Uncertainty generates the Quantum set in the simplest Bell scenario
papers.abstract: Characterizing the set of quantum nonlocal correlations through information-theoretic constraints is a central problem in quantum foundations. We show that the convex hull of no-signalling behaviors in a bipartite Bell experiment satisfying a common-overlap no-disturbance-without-uncertainty condition is exactly the finite-dimensional quantum set whenever one party has two binary measurements and the other has an arbitrary finite number of settings, each with an arbitrary finite number of outcomes. In the simplest binary input-output Bell scenario, this characterizes the full eight-dimensional set of quantum behaviors, including the local marginals. The proof constructs a quantum realization directly from the conditional probabilities and no-signalling. The characterization also reduces optimization of any linear Bell expression in these scenarios to maximization over a one-parameter family of second-order cone programs. The results establish a connection between local uncertainty-disturbance constraints and quantum nonlocality, mediated by no-signalling and shared classical randomness.
papers.authors: Ravishankar Ramanathan

papers.title: The parliament of observers - Against the observable axiom of quantum mechanics
papers.abstract: The 'unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics in the natural sciences' may at times give the impression that natural science, especially modern theoretical physics, is all but a formal apparatus. However, a key challenge of physics remains to align everyday notions of experience -- be it directly or mediated through instruments of arbitrary sophistication -- with their mathematical formalisation. This applies in particular to quantum theory, arguably the most successful theory of physics ever invented. One of its core assumptions postulates: $(Sharp)\ observables\ correspond\ with\ self-adjoint\ operators.$ Here, we argue that already this most basic premise about the quantum formalism falls apart under careful scrutiny, at least when understood for all observables at once. In other words, we challenge the role of the noncommutative algebra of bounded operators as an adequate formalisation of the 'algebra of observables', understood as (equivalence classes of) measurement procedures that admit a coherent empirical interpretation.
papers.authors: Markus Frembs, Andreas D\"oring

papers.title: The Mermin-Peres Magic Square Game With Three or More Players
papers.abstract: We present a generalization of the Mermin-Peres magic square game to $N$ players, in which the square is replaced by an $N$-dimensional hypercube. We show that the winning probability of the optimal classical strategy remains $8/9$ for all $N$, while for $N \ge 3$, a generalization of the quantum strategy for $N = 2$ achieves a winning probability between $1/3$ and $3/4$. This loss of quantum advantage for $N \ge 3$ is a consequence of monogamy.
papers.authors: Itamar Lorian, J. E. Avron

papers.title: Upper deviations of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick free energy: the fifth-order law and the onset of constrained Parisi measures
papers.abstract: Let $Z_N$ be the partition function of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at inverse temperature $\beta>1$. Replica theory (Kondor near the critical temperature, Parisi and Rizzo at all temperatures) predicts that the probability that $N^{-1}\log Z_N$ exceeds its typical value by $\delta$ decays like $\exp(-Na\delta^{6/5})$ with an explicit $a$; Aronow and Lopatto recently proved bounds of this order. The exponent is the Legendre transform of the Parisi problem constrained to carry an atom $\theta$ at zero. We show that the constrained minimum exceeds the equilibrium free energy by $c_\beta\theta^5(1+o(1))$, where $c_\beta=\frac{9}{640}\beta^3\rho_\beta(0)^{-3}$ and $\rho_\beta(0)>0$ is the density at zero of the Parisi measure. With the fractional-moment formula this gives the exponent $\frac56(6c_\beta)^{-1/5}\delta^{6/5}(1+o(1))$ as $N\to\infty$ and then $\delta\to0$. The constrained minimizer has a marginal first positive contact, to leading order at $3\theta/(2\rho_\beta(0))$ with an atom $\theta/2$. This plateau calculus applies to every mixture with $\xi'''(0)=0$ whose Parisi measure accumulates at zero; a small field $h$ opens a gap of order $|h|^{2/3}$, and an atom of the Parisi measure at zero, present in every pure $p$-spin model with $p\ge3$, makes the rate leave zero linearly. Near criticality the constant tends to Kondor's value $9/5120$ and the marginal regime ends at a de Almeida-Thouless threshold. For the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model at every $\beta>1$, a finite-step curvature inequality from an unrefereed preprint shows that every constrained minimizer either has an interval of positive contacts, all marginal, or has exactly two atoms, and that the marginal regime ends at a unique de Almeida-Thouless threshold $\theta_c(\beta)$. The laws at every $\beta>1$ use that the Parisi measure accumulates at zero, a theorem of Lopatto also proved in earlier work of the author.
papers.authors: Yan Ru Pei

papers.title: Quenched Growth of Normal Matrices and Harmonic Measure
papers.abstract: The eigenvalues of a large normal random matrix form a two-dimensional Coulomb gas. At fixed weight, the spectral droplet grows with the matrix rank, and its semiclassical density increment is harmonic measure. We freeze an $N$-eigenvalue configuration and sample $M$ further eigenvalues using the projection onto polynomials of degree less than $N+M$ that vanish at the frozen points. Their conditional law is an exact polynomial ensemble in the potential of the frozen charges. For a regular analytic droplet, we prove that the spatial distribution of the new eigenvalues converges to harmonic measure on the old boundary when $M/\log N\to\infty$ and $M/N\to0$. This convergence holds conditionally on the frozen spectrum, outside a set of frozen configurations whose probability tends to zero. The equilibrium process formed from orthogonal polynomials of degrees $N,\ldots,N+M-1$ has the same limit. An exact finite-rank identity relates polynomial moments of the conditional mean to fluctuations of the frozen spectrum, with a remainder from polynomial modes of degree $N+M$ and above.
papers.authors: Oleg Alekseev

papers.title: Mirror symmetry for gCICY threefolds (II): $[3,-1]$ blocks, VGIT, and toric phases
papers.abstract: We study mirror symmetry for a class of generalized complete intersection Calabi-Yau (gCICY) threefolds via variations of GIT. Our focus is on gCICY threefolds in $\mathbb{P}^1\times B$ with a $[3,-1]$ block, cut out by sections of $O(3)\boxtimes O_B(L)$ and $O(-1)\boxtimes O_B(L+R)$, where $B$ is a smooth projective fourfold and $2L+R=-K_B$. Auxiliary variables turn the generalized section into a relative variation of GIT, whose two phases are the gCICY threefold itself and the zero locus of a rank-3 bundle on $\mathbb{P}^2\times B$, and they are isomorphic or related by $\int_B L^4$ disjoint Atiyah flops. Over products of projective spaces, there are 18 Calabi-Yau threefold configurations with a $[3,-1]$ block. All of them except the non-Gorenstein case studied in the companion paper have toric phases with Gorenstein ambient spaces and nef partitions, so that after the variation of GIT their mirror symmetry reduces to Batyrev-Borisov duality. We analyze four examples with a $[3,-1]$ block and one outside this class in detail.
papers.authors: Atsushi Kanazawa

papers.title: Root-sparsity scaling for Hamiltonian simulation, differential equations and linear-system solvers
papers.abstract: We give quantum algorithms for time-independent and time-dependent Hamiltonian simulation, linear differential equations and linear systems, all with complexity that has only square-root dependence on matrix sparsity. Our algorithms retain optimal scaling in other relevant parameters such as time, condition number and precision. For several cases we prove matching lower bounds on the joint parameters and show that the additional gate overhead is only polylogarithmic in the inverse precision. The common primitive connecting our algorithms is the Cayley transform, which provides a cheap unitary embedding of the sparse matrices. For Hamiltonian simulation and differential equations, we then use transducers to construct the desired evolution operators. For linear systems, we instead encode the solution in the kernel of a matrix and use the Cayley transform to construct a projector onto that kernel.
papers.authors: Dominic W. Berry, Abhishek Rawat, Sophia Simon, Guang Hao Low

papers.title: Sparse Hamiltonian simulation with optimal dependence on the maximum column Euclidean norm
papers.abstract: We give a quantum algorithm for simulating a $d$-sparse Hermitian Hamiltonian $H$, assuming known upper bounds $\Lambda$ on its maximum column Euclidean norm $\|H\|_{1\to2}$ and $\Lambda_{\max}$ on its maximum entry magnitude. For every $t\ge0$, simulation with operator-norm error $\epsilon$ uses \[ O\!\left(t\Lambda\sqrt d +\sqrt{td\Lambda_{\max}\log(2/\epsilon)}+\log(2/\epsilon)\right) \] sparse-oracle queries. This removes the subpolynomial overhead in Low's algorithm [STOC 2019]. For $d>1$ and $t\Lambda\ge\log(2/\epsilon)$, the bound matches the worst-case lower bound. A known spectral-norm upper bound may also be used in place of $\Lambda$. The number of 1- and 2-qubit gates is linear in the query scale, up to oracle costs and polynomial overhead in the input bit lengths and logarithmic precision parameters. As applications, we obtain $O(\kappa\sqrt d\,\mathrm{polylog}(\kappa/\epsilon))$ queries for solving $d$-sparse quantum linear systems with $\|A\|\le1$ and $\|A^{-1}\|\le\kappa$, under standard sparse and state-preparation access. We also give a gate-efficient implementation of black-box unitaries with at most $d$ nonzero entries per row and column using $O(\sqrt{d\log(2/\epsilon)}+\log(2/\epsilon))$ queries, given sparse access to the unitary and its adjoint. At constant error, the query bound is optimal and yields $\Theta(\sqrt N)$ queries for arbitrary $N\times N$ unitaries, resolving the open question on black-box unitary implementation posed by Berry and Childs [QIC 2012].
papers.authors: Zecheng Li, Chunhao Wang

papers.title: Local Automorphism-Aware Syndrome Compilation for General Quantum LDPC Codes
papers.abstract: Low-depth syndrome extraction for Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) quantum low-density parity-check codes can be formulated as a proper ordered edge-coloring problem subject to quantum parity constraints. A proper edge-coloring of the CSS Tanner graph ensures that each data or ancilla qubit participates in at most one two-qubit gate per layer, but does not guarantee a valid interleaving of the X- and Z-check measurements as for every overlapping X/Z check pair, the number of shared data qubits on which the X interaction precedes the Z interaction must be even. The minimum number of colors in a proper ordered edge-coloring satisfying the quantum parity constraints equals the minimum two-qubit depth when each stabilizer check is measured with a single ancilla. We introduce local automorphism-aware syndrome compilation (LocalASC), which reduces the constraint system to edge-orbit variables under a subgroup of the Tanner graph automorphisms and lifts each feasible orbit assignment to the full graph. Although the $6$-layer degree lower bound is unattainable for the published weight-$6$ IBM bivariate bicycle codes, we show that this is not universal among two-block CSS codes. Among code instances for which the maximum check weight equals the maximum Tanner graph degree, LocalASC finds depth-optimal syndrome-extraction schedules for several two-block CSS codes with odd component weights, including instances with unequal odd weights. We also obtain lower-bound-saturating syndrome-extraction schedules for several quantum Tanner codes satisfying the same degree condition. To obtain the subgroups used by LocalASC without computing the full automorphism group of the Tanner graph, we construct translation subgroups for two-block group-algebra CSS codes over abelian groups. For quantum Tanner codes, we give conditions under which square-complex symmetries extend to Tanner graph automorphisms.
papers.authors: Eugenio Durazo Rocha, Olai \AA. Mostad, Hsuan-Yin Lin, Eirik Rosnes

papers.title: AI for BMN Strings
papers.abstract: With the assistance of AI (Artificial Intelligence) tools, we revisit some mathematically well-formulated problems from our previous studies of BMN (Berenstein-Maldacena-Nastase) strings on type IIB string theory pp-wave background. These mathematical problems have important physical implications, relating to the computations of higher-genus critical superstring amplitudes, possible estimate of the cosmological constant. We make significant progress on some problems, while others remain unresolved.
papers.authors: Min-xin Huang

papers.title: Continuum Limit for One-Dimensional Moir\'e Relaxation
papers.abstract: We establish convergence of minimizers for a minimal one dimensional atomic-scale model for relaxation in moir\'e materials to those of a one-dimensional continuum limit functional analogous to those commonly used in practice to model relaxation. The atomic-scale model consists of two periodic chains containing $N$ and $N+1$ atoms per common cell and is exactly moir\'e-periodic at the atomic scale. Its energy combines harmonic nearest-neighbor intralayer interactions with nonlocal interlayer interactions generated by an even $C^2$ pair potential with polynomial decay. The associated continuum energy couples linear elasticity to a periodic misfit potential, obtained by periodizing the pair potential, which penalizes unfavorable local stackings.
papers.authors: Hao Lan, Michael Hott, Jeff Calder, Alexander B. Watson

papers.title: Quantum Complexity of Ancilla-Free Unitary Embeddings for Nonlinear Dynamics via Generalized State-Dependent Double-Bracket Flows
papers.abstract: Simulating nonlinear dynamics with quantum computers has gained increasing attention. In general, such simulations require additional quantum resources because unitary quantum evolution is linear. A fundamental question is how nonlinear dynamics can be embedded into fully coherent, ancilla-free unitary circuits and how the complexity of the dynamics governs the required quantum resources. In this work, we generalize the ancilla-free double-bracket quantum algorithm for imaginary-time evolution by replacing its state-independent Hamiltonian with a state-dependent Hermitian operator. Our framework recursively calls an initial state preparation oracle and its inverse, and prepares the target solution to any prescribed accuracy using a fully coherent, ancilla-free unitary embedding. We relate the query cost to the complexity of the nonlinear dynamics, specifically their sensitivity to initial conditions. We obtain query upper bounds of $\exp(O(T))$, $\exp(O(T^2))$, and $\exp(\exp(O(T)))$ when the distance between solutions contracts at least exponentially (contractive), does not increase (nonexpansive), or grows at most exponentially (expansive), respectively, where $T$ is the target evolution time. For the discrete Gross--Pitaevskii equation, our ancilla-free double-bracket circuit achieves optimal worst-case query complexity $\Theta(e^{gT/2})$ over a specified family of single-qubit initial states, where $g>0$ is the nonlinearity strength. These results connect the complexity of nonlinear dynamics to the query cost of coherent quantum simulation and provide a foundation for designing ancilla-free unitary embeddings with optimal query complexity.
papers.authors: Yuki Ito, Hideaki Hakoshima, Keisuke Fujii

papers.title: Black objects in a five-dimensional swirling spacetime
papers.abstract: We use the Ehlers symmetry of the five-dimensional Ernst equation to embed the Myers-Perry black hole and the rotating black ring in a five-dimensional swirling spacetime. We show that both solutions can be made free of conical singularities, and that the swirl modifies the balance condition of the black ring. We compute horizon areas, surface gravities and Komar charges, which satisfy a Smarr relation, and study the ergoregions.
papers.authors: Adriano Vigan\`o

papers.title: Nash Equilibrium from Quantum-Field Entanglement
papers.abstract: Entanglement harvesting allows localized probes to extract entanglement from a quantum field, even when their interaction regions are spacelike separated. However, how the resource obtained by the probes can be operationalized remains largely open. In this work, we ask whether the harvested entanglement can influence the timing choices of observers acting as players. We construct a quantum input game for Alice and Bob, each controlling an Unruh-DeWitt detector that couples to the vacuum of a free massless scalar field in four-dimensional Minkowski spacetime. Each player can choose an early interaction time, a late interaction time, or exit. After joint entry, a referee sends independent question qubits, so that fixed local Bell measurements and a payment table convert the detector state into a payoff. The mean payoff is proportional to minus the expectation value of an entanglement witness and is nonpositive for every separable resource. We calculate the detector state to leading perturbative order and solve the participation game analytically. Away from payoff degeneracies, every timing equilibrium with positive payoff gives two trembling hand perfect participation equilibria, in addition to mutual exit. The total count can therefore be one, three, five, or seven. For one fixed switching function and timing menu, five selected delays give the sequence seven, three, one, seven, and one. The timing payoffs follow from the field's two-point functions, with the Hadamard and Pauli-Jordan contributions to the coherence competing against local excitation noise. The resulting equilibrium structure provides an operational setting for studying how vacuum correlations and causal propagation affect the strategic use of quantum-field entanglement.
papers.authors: Hao Xu

papers.title: A Three-Party W-State Quantum Secret Sharing Protocol with X-Gate Encoding and Forbidden-Outcome Detection
papers.abstract: We propose a new three-party quantum secret sharing (QSS) protocol based on a three-qubit W state for distributing a predetermined sequence of classical bits. Alice encodes each bit using X gates and randomly applies Hadamard gates to the transmitted qubits. Her Hadamard-gate choices and the measurement bases independently chosen by Bob and Charlie determine the type of each round (information, test or semi-information) during transmission, without designating test rounds in advance. Suitable semi-information rounds provide additional opportunities for secret transmission and improve efficiency. The protocol combines secret transmission and tests for forbidden outcomes within the same ensemble of encoded W states. In the ideal model without an attack, transmitting an n-bit secret requires an average of 3n protocol rounds, giving a qubit efficiency of 1/9. We analyze intercept-and-resend and entangle-and-measure attacks by an internal adversary and derive their single-round and cumulative detection probabilities. For the entangle-and-measure attack, we relate the information obtainable through an ancillary system to the probability of forbidden test outcomes. The protocol is implemented in Python using Qiskit and evaluated through ideal simulation and experiments on IBM Quantum hardware. The simulation results are consistent with the theoretical predictions, while hardware measurements characterize round efficiency, reconstruction errors, forbidden-outcome probabilities and the information obtained through the specified ancilla measurement. A calibrated statistical criterion accounts for forbidden outcomes caused by hardware noise, with detection and false-alarm probabilities evaluated using a binomial model with measured rates. This analysis connects the ideal protocol predictions with a finite-sample assessment under the specified attack models and statistical assumptions.
papers.authors: Timur R. Teregulov, Elena R. Loubenets

papers.title: Encrypted Quantum Cloning Beyond Maximal Entanglement: Exact Classification of Multipartite Resources
papers.abstract: Encrypted quantum cloning distributes an unknown $k$-qubit state among $m$ individually concealed signals, each permitting exact recovery when combined with a common quantum key. While canonical constructions rely on maximally entangled resources, they do not establish which multipartite states are necessary or sufficient for this task. Here we derive necessary and sufficient conditions characterizing all pure resources compatible with a prescribed sector-wise two-Pauli encoder for $m\geq 2$, with necessity holding for arbitrary completely positive trace-preserving recovery maps. The classification reveals a sharp parity dependence: even $m$ requires maximal signal--key entanglement, whereas odd $m$ admits nonmaximally entangled resources when their residual signal correlations belong to an encoder-selected commuting algebra. Beyond this architecture, we show that exact recovery from every authorized subsystem under arbitrary unitary encoders acting on the input and signals while leaving the key untouched necessarily implies perfect individual concealment, requires at least $(m-1)k$ ebits of signal--key entanglement, and imposes spectral constraints on the resource. For graph states, the classification reduces to an exact cut-kernel criterion, enabling binary certification and constructive Clifford recovery. In particular, a rank-deficient three-output resource in the YZ/ZY branch attains the general entanglement lower bound with two ebits rather than three. We also exclude the entire Dicke family, including $W$ states, within the two-Pauli architecture. Together, these results distinguish fundamental entanglement requirements from encoder-dependent correlation constraints, providing an exact characterization of resource admissibility and a constructive recovery framework for graph states.
papers.authors: Pritam Roy, Shashank Gupta

papers.title: Revisiting the Frolov--Zelnikov solution for Majumdar--Papapetrou black holes
papers.abstract: We revisit Frolov and Zelnikov's electrostatic Green function for a test charge in a multi-center Majumdar--Papapetrou spacetime, correcting its horizon-charge condition and extending the result to higher dimensions. In four dimensions, we derive the exact Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for a minimally coupled spectator Maxwell field with independently prescribed horizon potentials. The horizon flux charges obey a capacitance matrix with entries $C_{AA}=M_A+\sum_{B\ne A}M_AM_B/R_{AB}$ and $C_{AB}=-M_AM_B/R_{AB}$, where $M_A$ are center masses and $R_{AB}$ their separations. This matrix is a positive diagonal term plus a weighted graph Laplacian, yielding an exact common-mode/differential-mode decomposition of the field energy. The grounded Dirichlet Green function partitions a point charge's flux among infinity and the horizons through harmonic measures. We show that the diagonal condition imposed by Frolov and Zelnikov [Eq.~(4.14)] preserves only the total horizon charge, allowing redistribution between individual horizons. A corrected symmetric Green function preserving each horizon charge instead involves the inverse capacitance matrix. For two centers, the correction produces a finite, negative-semidefinite self-energy shift and an exact self-force difference, without additional ultraviolet subtraction. Finally, we extend the capacitance matrix, flux partition, and fixed-charge Green function to $D=n+3$ dimensions, where the graph weights contain the universal factor $\pi^{n/2}/\Gamma(n/2)$.
papers.authors: Jongheon Baek, Gihwan Nam

papers.title: Grothendieck rings of strictly weakly integral fusion categories of rank six
papers.abstract: We classify, up to based-ring isomorphism, the Grothendieck rings of strictly weakly integral fusion categories of rank six over $\mathbb C$. The dimension grading and the classification of integral Grothendieck rings of rank at most five reduce the problem to twelve candidate fusion rings. We exclude four of them using the twist trace and the induction pairing in the Drinfeld center. The remaining eight admit known categorifications. In particular, every such category has commutative Grothendieck ring and Frobenius--Perron dimension in $\{8,10,16,20\}$.
papers.authors: Kai Wang, Jingcheng Dong, Libin Li

papers.title: Lyapunov-controlled thermalization: an exact real-time example
papers.abstract: A verified Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) relation, after a drive has ceased, is not sufficient evidence to prove equilibrium. We demonstrate this in a large-$N$ large-$q$ Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) quench protocol. Although all post-quench fermion correlators are exactly thermal, a second quench back to the initial Hamiltonian reveals hidden memory of the initial state. It is encoded in correlators connecting to times before the first quench. This memory is an extensive nonequilibrium (NEQ) witness with its decay rate being the Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_L$. Thus $\lambda_L$ sets the rate at which the state becomes effectively indistinguishable from a Gibbs state. Despite being a unitary interacting many-body system, the complete NEQ real-time evolution is obtained exactly in the large-$N$, large-$q$ limit, making the setup ideal for analytically studying thermalization.
papers.authors: Jonas Loy, Jan C. Louw

papers.title: Matter Swapping between Two Branes: Conditions for a Local Type IIB D3-D7-D3 Mechanism of Charged-Fermion Mixing via E3 Instantons
papers.abstract: Effective infrared two-sheeted descriptions of fermion mixing between braneworlds have emerged in several distinct realizations and lead to testable matter-swapping effects, motivating low-energy searches and cosmological applications. The recurrence of the same low-energy fermion operator motivates investigating whether this structure can also arise from a D-brane mechanism. We investigate the conditions under which a local Type IIB D3$_+$-D7-D3$_-$/E3 configuration can generate perturbatively forbidden interbrane mixing. Assuming the required charged zero-mode spectrum, neutral instanton measure and non-vanishing charged disk amplitudes, we derive an E3-induced chiral mass term with scalar and pseudoscalar components. The latter reproduces the characteristic mixing structure of the two-sheeted fermion operator, while D7 Wilson transport supplies the gauge-invariant relative connection between the two brane sectors. We establish the corresponding gauge matching for transitions between stationary states at resonance. This yields a conditional matching to the two-sheeted operator within the effective field theory. A separate orbifold example checks the charged zero-mode representations and the compensating instanton charge. Whether all the required instanton ingredients coexist with two independent massive D3-D7 matter sectors at separated endpoints in a single local configuration remains open. We outline a model-building roadmap toward such a configuration and its compact phenomenological embedding. Such an embedding requires electromagnetic sequestering of the two fermion sectors and a sufficiently light non-uniform D7 gauge mode mediating a long-range relative interaction. In such a compactification, the mixing parameter $g$ would be determined by microscopic instanton data and matter-field normalization, providing a connection to low-energy constraints.
papers.authors: Micha\"el Sarrazin

papers.title: A complete classification of the existence of finite-dimensional quantum solutions to inconsistent linear constraint systems
papers.abstract: Linear constraint systems (LCS) provide a compact algebraic language for nonlocal games and state-independent contextuality. In the binary case the Mermin--Peres square shows that inconsistent LCS can be solved by promoting variables to local Pauli operators, whereas a series of no-go results excludes analogous Pauli-, Clifford- and monomial unitary-based constructions at odd prime modulus. We first isolate the reason for this difference: for tensor-product quantum solutions, the obstruction to a classical solution of a LCS over $\mathbb{Z}_n$ decomposes into obstruction classes carried by the individual factors. As a consequence, a genuinely global obstruction cannot arise solely by tensoring locally unobstructed systems. The argument is specific to odd modulus; at even modulus the reordering phase need not vanish, as in Pauli-based examples. Given this distinction, we instead associate LCS to finite arrangements of rank-one projectors and resolutions of the identity in finite-dimensional vector spaces. Quantum solvability for such LCS is automatic and the search for a quantum-classical gap rests entirely on proving classical unsatisfiability of the underlying modular incidence problem of the arrangement. By relating such LCS with group-valued frame functions, we identify a family of examples in the work of [Harding, Jager, and Smith, Int. J. Theor. Phys. 44, 539 (2005)]. To establish the (non)existence of classically unsatisfiable LCS over $\mathbb{Z}_n$ with quantum solutions in all dimensions $d$ and for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, we further construct explicit examples for the cases $d=n$ prime. Our main result thus positively resolves the existence problem of such LCS beyond the binary case: such systems exist if and only if $d\geq 3$ and $\gcd(n,d)>1$. Moreover, we establish the existence of LCS with a quantum-classical gap over finite fields if and only if $d\geq 3$ and $p\mid d$.
papers.authors: Markus Frembs

papers.title: Feature-Adaptive Fusion in Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Networks for Robust Biomedical Image Classification
papers.abstract: Hybrid quantum--classical neural networks offer a promising framework for integrating quantum circuits into machine learning in the noisy intermediate-scale quantum era. However, fixed or globally shared fusion strategies used in many existing hybrid models may limit the effective integration of complementary classical and quantum information. To address this limitation, we propose a Feature-Adaptive Fusion Hybrid Quantum--Classical Neural Network (FAF-HQNN) for biomedical image classification. The proposed model combines a classical deep feature encoder with a variational quantum circuit (VQC) and employs a feature-adaptive fusion mechanism to dynamically weight classical and quantum predictions across samples and classes. Under the evaluated settings, FAF-HQNN achieves competitive accuracy on PathMNIST and BloodMNIST compared to internal variants and external hybrid quantum--classical baselines. On PathMNIST, FAF-HQNN achieves higher aggregate mean accuracy than all evaluated baselines under both Gaussian and Poisson noise. These results suggest that feature-adaptive fusion may help improve classification performance within the evaluated framework.
papers.authors: Yan-Yan Hou, Jian Li, Chongqiang Ye, Hengji Li, Zhuo Wang, Qinghui Liu

papers.title: Universal Defect Statistics in Reverse Quenches
papers.abstract: We extend the generalized Kibble-Zurek mechanism (gKZM) to reverse quench protocols using a stochastic description of defect formation finding that the mean defect density after a reverse quench equals twice the forward quench defect-number variance per unit volume. This relation, universally valid within the stochastic framework of the gKZM, makes the forward quench variance accessible through a reverse quench defect density measurement. We verify the equality analytically and numerically in the uniform one-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, and numerically in its bond-disordered variant, including a regime where defect scaling departs from a pure power-law in quench time. Our result also suggests an experimental route to probing quantum critical behavior: reverse quenches that begin and end in the paramagnetic phase may allow to reveal critical exponents using global magnetic-field control and magnetization measurements, without resolving individual defects.
papers.authors: Eduard J. Braun, Daniel Rubin, Margaux Cartier, Gerhard Z\"urn, Matthias Weidem\"uller

papers.title: Universal Structure of Horizon Formation in Generic Binary Black Hole Mergers
papers.abstract: A new common apparent horizon forms during a binary black hole merger and gives rise to outer and inner branches of marginally outer trapped surfaces. We derive the local structure of these branches. This event occurs in the fully nonlinear regime, outside the standard regimes of post-Newtonian inspiral theory and perturbations of a stationary black hole, yet it admits a universal description. Without assuming symmetry, we show that the stability operator of the marginally outer trapped surface must lose invertibility at formation. Outermost stability then implies that the vanishing eigenvalue is the principal one, with a strictly positive eigenfunction. Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction yields square-root branch separation with a shared linear drift. The outer and inner common horizons lie on a smooth marginally outer trapped tube along which slice time has a local minimum at formation, and nearby later slices intersect it in outer and inner branches whose separation scales as $(t-t_*)^{1/2}$. Sufficiently smooth quasilocal scalar functionals with nonzero first variation along the principal zero mode inherit the square-root separation and a shared linear term. We test these predictions in three binary black hole simulations, including an eccentric, precessing, unequal-mass system. In all three, the worldtube geometry and quasilocal scalars follow the predicted scaling. With the next-order term included, free-exponent fits to the surface geometry and quasilocal functionals recover the square-root exponent, $1/2$, to within half a percent, and diagnostics agree on the formation time within $5\times10^{-5}M$. The correlation between horizon shear and gravitational-wave news raises the possibility that common horizon formation has a signature in a short segment of the merger waveform.
papers.authors: Yu-Cun Xie, Vaishak Prasad

papers.title: Alternative Boundary Conditions in Asymptotically Anti-de Sitter Spacetimes
papers.abstract: Anti-de Sitter (AdS) spacetimes are not globally hyperbolic, so boundary conditions are generally needed for well-defined dynamics. Ishibashi and Wald (IW) determined boundary conditions yielding well-posed dynamics with conserved positive energy for scalar, electromagnetic, and linearized gravitational fields, using nonlocal potentials and individual spherical harmonic modes. In this paper, we determine which IW conditions are local in the primary fields and which are AdS-invariant.
