Quantum generative adversarial networks (QGANs) provide a powerful framework for learning unitary dynamics, often achieving more compact representations than standard Trotter-based approaches. However, their practical performance is frequently limited by optimization plateaus and suboptimal local minima. Here, we propose an entanglement-assisted learning strategy that mitigates these bottlenecks by dynamically coupling the system during training to a randomly initialized auxiliary system. This temporary enlargement of the Hilbert space redistributes quantum correlations and improves trainability. We numerically demonstrate its advantage in learning Hamiltonian dynamics with a hardware-efficient ansatz. By analyzing connectivity, coupling timing, and parameter initialization of the auxiliary system, we identify the key ingredients behind the observed performance gains. Our results highlight a strategy for overcoming optimization bottlenecks in variational quantum algorithms, with applications in quantum simulation, quantum control, and quantum machine learning.
papers.authors: Ayaka Usui, Guillermo Abad-L\'opez, Hari krishnan SV, Anna Sanpera, Some Sankar Bhattacharya

papers.title: Topology of the Fermi surface and universality of the metal-metal and metal-insulator transitions: $d$-dimensional Hatsugai-Kohmoto model as an example
papers.abstract: The earlier theory \cite{Chitov:2025} of the quantum phase transitions related to the change of the Fermi Surface Topology (FST) is advanced. For such transitions the Fermi surface as a quantum critical manifold determined by the Lee-Yang zeros, the order parameter $\mathcal{P}$ as the $d$-volume of the Fermi sea, and the special FST universality class were introduced in \cite{Chitov:2025}. The exactly solvable Hatsugai-Kohmoto (HK) $d$-dimensional ($d=1,2,3$) model of interacting fermions is analyzed. We explore the relation between the Lee-Yang zeros, the Luttinger and the plateau (Oshikawa) theorems. The validity of the Luttinger theorem in the HK model is confirmed. It is shown that the order parameter $\mathcal{P}$ and the FST universality class describe the transitions between metal and band/Mott insulators, as well as the Lifshitz and van Hove gapless-to-gapless transitions. The gapless phases are established to be the ferromagnetic Fermi liquids (metals), where the quantum critical manifold is also a locus of ferromagnetic order with spontaneous breaking of the rotational symmetry occurring at $T=0$. In addition to the conventional paradigm with a continuous order parameter, we apply the homology theory to analyze the FST transitions. They are critical points of the Morse function. To quantify FST we use the Euler characteristic, which is calculated for each phase of the HK model. We claim that the FST universality class is robust with respect to interactions and other model details, under the condition that the conduction band function is smooth and the critical points are non-degenerate.
papers.authors: Gennady Y. Chitov

papers.title: Protocols for a many-body phase microscope: From coherences and d-wave superconductivity to Green's functions
papers.abstract: Quantum gas microscopes probe quantum many-body lattice states via projective measurements in the occupation basis, enabling access to various density and spin correlations. Phase information, however, cannot be directly obtained in these setups. Recent experiments went beyond this by measuring local current operators and local phase fluctuations. Here we propose how Fourier-space manipulation in a matter-wave microscope allows access to various long-range off-diagonal correlators in experimentally realistic settings, realizing a many-body phase microscope. We demonstrate in particular how the fermionic d-wave superconducting order parameter in arbitrary Hubbard-type models, the non-equal time Green's function yielding the spectral function, or the hidden order of composite bosons in a fractional Chern insulator can be directly measured. Our results show the great potential of matter-wave microscopy for accessing exotic correlators including phases and coherences and characterizing intriguing quantum many-body states.
papers.authors: Christof Weitenberg, Luca Asteria, Ola Carlsson, Annabelle Bohrdt, Fabian Grusdt

papers.title: A new product formula for $(z;q)_\infty$, with applications to asymptotics
papers.abstract: We express the $q$-Pochhammer symbol $(z;q)_\infty$ as an infinite product of gamma functions, analogously to how Narukawa expressed the elliptic gamma function as an infinite product of hyperbolic gamma functions. This identity is used to obtain asymptotic expansions when $q$ tends to $1$.
papers.authors: Arash Arabi Ardehali, Hjalmar Rosengren

papers.title: Characterizing the Trainability of Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial Circuit Born Machines
papers.abstract: Instantaneous Quantum Polynomial Circuit Born Machines (IQP-QCBMs) have been proposed as quantum generative models that combine a classically tractable training objective - based on the maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) - with a potential quantum advantage motivated by sampling-complexity arguments. While recent works have explored this model across various application domains, fundamental questions remain: does the model suffer from exponentially vanishing loss gradients, known as the barren plateau problem - a pervasive obstacle in quantum machine learning - and how do regimes of trainability relate to regimes of possible quantum advantage? Here, we address both questions analytically. To study trainability, we derive closed-form expressions for the variances of the partial derivatives of the MMD loss function and establish general upper and lower bounds. We explicitly characterize how trainability depends on the generator set and the spectrum of the chosen kernel, identifying regimes in which low Hamming-weight kernels avoid exponential gradient suppression under structured topologies. Regarding potential quantum advantage, we reformulate the anti-concentration property in terms of the same generator-set quantities that govern trainability, enabling a unified analysis. We show that sparse IQP architectures can produce classically intractable output distributions while simultaneously remaining trainable, at least at lower-weight frequencies. Our analytical results corroborate the numerical observations of prior work and provide principled guidelines for designing scalable IQP-QCBM architectures.
papers.authors: Kevin Shen, Susanne Pielawa, Vedran Dunjko, Hao Wang

papers.title: Resummed energy loss in extreme-mass-ratio scattering using critical orbits
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent efforts to bridge between weak-field and strong-field descriptions of black-hole binary dynamics, we develop a resummation scheme for post-Minkowskian radiative observables in extreme-mass-ratio scattering, augmented with post-Newtonian terms. Specifically, we derive universal interpolation formulas for the total energy emitted in gravitational waves out to infinity and down the event horizon of the large black hole, valid to leading order in the small mass ratio. We test our formulas using numerical results from direct calculations in black hole perturbation theory. The central idea of our approach is to utilize as a strong-field diagnostic the known form of divergence in the radiated energy along geodesics near the parameter-space separatrix between scattering and plunge. The dominant, logarithmic term of this divergence can be expressed in terms of instantaneous energy fluxes calculated along the unstable circular geodesics that form the separatrix, fluxes that we obtain using interpolation of highly accurate numerical data. The same idea could be applied to bound-orbit radiative observables via either unbound-to-bound mapping or a direct resummation of bound-orbit post-Newtonian expressions.
papers.authors: Leor Barack, Riccardo Gonzo, Benjamin Leather, Oliver Long, Niels Warburton

papers.title: Information-Theoretic Gaps in Solar and Reactor Neutrino Oscillation Measurements
papers.abstract: Quantum estimation theory provides a fundamental framework for analyzing how precisely physical parameters can be estimated from measurements. Neutrino oscillations are characterized by a set of parameters inferred from experiments conducted in different production and detection environments. The two solar oscillation parameters, $\Delta m^2_{21}$ and $\theta_{12}$, can be estimated using both solar neutrino experiments and reactor neutrino experiments. In this letter, we use Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) to quantify and compare the information content accessible in these two experimental setups. For reactor neutrinos, flavor measurements saturate the QFI for both parameters over relevant energy ranges, demonstrating that ideal measurements could achieve ultimate quantum precision bound. In contrast, for solar neutrinos the phase-based QFI vanishes, originating from the quantum coherence, rendering the estimation of $\Delta m_{21}^2$ purely population-based and effectively classical, while the QFI for $\theta_{12}$ remains sizable and nearly saturated by flavor measurements at high energies. Consequently, solar experiments are intrinsically more sensitive to $\theta_{12}$ than to $\Delta m_{21}^2$, reflecting a fundamental difference in the information encoded in the two systems.
papers.authors: Neetu Raj Singh Chundawat, Yu-Feng Li

papers.title: Quantum randomness under unambiguous attacks
papers.abstract: Intrinsic randomness is generated when a quantum state is measured in any basis in which it is not diagonal. In an adversarial scenario, we quantify this randomness by the probability that a correlated eavesdropper could correctly guess the measurement outcomes. What if the eavesdropper is never wrong, but can sometimes return an inconclusive outcome? Inspired by analogous concepts in quantum state discrimination, we consider the randomness generated by a measurement setup when an eavesdropper guesses unambiguously, and, relaxing the assumption of perfect accuracy, with a fixed rate of inconclusive outcomes. We solve the maximal randomness of any quantum state under an unambiguous or FRIO attack, optimized over all projective measurements. We also solve both problems for any state and projective measurement in dimension two. If a noisy setup is used to choose random bases for a prepare-and-measure quantum key distribution protocol, an unambiguous attack may allow an eavesdropper to gain knowledge about the secret key, without causing any disturbance. Moreover, while experimental noise is typically ascribed to a single device, we find, given a state measured in an unbiased basis of any dimension, that an eavesdropper correlated only to a noisy state is outperformed by an eavesdropper with joint correlations to both a noisy state and a noisy measurement. In fact, we identify a critical noise parameter beyond which the joint-noise eavesdropper achieves a perfect guessing probability, ending all hopes of private randomness.
papers.authors: Fionnuala Curran

papers.title: Fractional Quantum Hall States: Infinite Matrix Product Representation and its Implications
papers.abstract: We present a novel matrix product representation of the Laughlin and related fractional quantum Hall wavefunctions based on a rigorous version of the correlators of a chiral quantum field theory. This representation enables the quantitative control of the coefficients of the Laughlin wavefunction times an arbitrary monomial symmetric polynomial when expanded in a Slater determinant or permanent basis. It renders the properties, such as factorization and the renewal structure, inherent in such fractional quantum Hall wavefunctions transparent. We prove bounds on the correlators of the chiral quantum field theory and utilize this representation to demonstrate the exponential decay of connected correlations and a gap in the entanglement spectrum on a thin cylinder.
papers.authors: Severin Schraven, Simone Warzel

papers.title: On theta function expressions of cyclic products of fermion correlation functions in genus two
papers.abstract: In arXiv:2211.09069, significant progress was made in decomposing simple products of fermion correlation functions, and in summing over spin structures of superstring amplitudes in genus two under cyclic constraints. In this manuscript we consider part of the same subject using a framework in which one of the branch points of the genus two curve is fixed at infinity. This framework is a direct generalization of the popular one in the case of genus one. We address some of the issues that remained unresolved in our previous paper arXiv:2209.14633. We show that the spin structures of the simple products of fermion correlation functions with cyclic conditions depend only on the Pe-function values at the half-periods of the genus two surface, for any number of factors in the products. Similar to the genus one case, we can provide basis functions to decompose the product. Consequently, the trilinear relations found in arXiv:2211.09069 can be derived from the known set of differential equations of genus two Pe-functions by setting the variables equal to the half-periods of the non-singular and even spin structures, as is the case for genus one. Based on these considerations, we present a procedure for expressing the results of decomposed formulae in terms of the unique genus two theta function for two, three, and four point cases, and discuss a realistic approach for calculating six point function. A general formula for the expression of the results in terms of the theta function for the product of an arbitrary number of the fermion correlation functions is not yet derivable.
papers.authors: A. G. Tsuchiya

papers.title: Dynamical entanglement percolation with spatially correlated disorder
papers.abstract: The distribution of entanglement between the nodes of a quantum network plays a fundamental role in quantum information applications. In this work, we investigate the dynamics of a network of qubits where each edge corresponds to an independent two-qubit interaction. By applying tools from percolation theory, we study how long-range entanglement, obtained via singlet conversion and swapping from dynamically generated pairs, emerges across the network. We show that the interplay between unitary evolution and spatially correlated disorder leads to a non-standard percolation phenomenology, significantly richer than uniform bond percolation and featuring multi-valued hysteresis-like behaviour. A two-colour correlated bond percolation model, whose phase diagram is determined via numerical simulations and a mean-field theory, fully elucidates the physics behind this phenomenon.
papers.authors: Lorenzo Cirigliano, Valentina Brosco, Claudio Castellano, Simone Felicetti, Laura Pilozzi, Bernard van Heck

papers.title: Discrete gravitational diagram technique and corrections to the Newtonian potential
papers.abstract: To develop a gravitational diagram technique that is ultraviolet finite, we start from Regge's simplicial gravity and use a bell-shaped form of the measure obtained via functional integration over connection. A "hypercubic" structure is considered (some variables are frozen), it is described by the metric $g_{\lambda \mu}$ at the sites. The measure is known in closed form if the timelike length scale is fixed at a low level. This is possible in the synchronous gauge (properly softened to remove nonphysical infrared singularities). This gauge also allows, with a refined finite-difference form of the action, to match the analytical properties of the propagator to the continuum case. The metric is parameterized to make the measure Lebesgue. The linear part of this parametrization leads to a discrete form of standard Feynman diagrams that approximates finite continuum diagrams and is finite for infinite ones; the nonlinear part gives new vertices and diagrams. The maximum of the measure is at the edge length scale $b = b_{\rm s} \sim \eta^{1/2}$, where $\eta$ defines the free factor like $(- \det \|g_{\lambda \mu}\|)^{\eta/2}$ in the measure and should be a large parameter to ensure true action upon integration over connection. For general perturbative expansion (including both that for the measure and the S matrix) to be free of increasing powers of $\eta$, its initial point must be at $b$ sufficiently close to $b_{\rm s}$; this appears to be a dynamic mechanism for establishing $b$ as an optimal initial point of the perturbative expansion. This technique is applied to Newton's potential. Some of new diagrams, including potentially large ones, are mutually cancelled. The S matrix expansion is analyzed to consist of standard diagrams. These diagrams form series with a small parameter $\eta^{-1}$; one-loop diagrams calculated in the literature represent the leading order.
papers.authors: V. M. Khatsymovsky

papers.title: New Projection Operators for Planar Electrodynamics
papers.abstract: In this article, we provide a new construction of a set of projection operators and apply it to obtain the propagator of three-dimensional models of electrodynamics; in particular, we consider the Maxwell-Lee-Wick-Chern-Simons, Maxwell-Deser-Jackiw electrodynamics and nonlocal infinite derivative electrodynamics. In order to prove the efficacy of these operators, we perform a causality and unitarity analysis to investigate the presence of ghosts and tachyons.
papers.authors: Fl\'avio P. Cruz, Jos\'e A. Santos, Victor J. V. Otoya

papers.title: Highly resilient, error-protected quantum gates in a solid-state quantum network node
papers.abstract: High-fidelity quantum gates are the cornerstone of any quantum computing and communications architecture. Realizing such control in the presence of realistic errors at the level required for beyond-threshold quantum error correction is a long-standing challenge for all quantum hardware platforms. Here we theoretically develop and experimentally demonstrate error-protected quantum gates in a solid-state quantum network node. Our work combines room-temperature randomized benchmarking with a new class of composite pulses that are simultaneously robust to frequency and amplitude, affecting random and systematic errors. We introduce Power-Unaffected, Doubly-Detuning-INsensitive Gates (PUDDINGs) - a theoretical framework for constructing conditional gates with immunity to both amplitude and frequency errors. For single-qubit and two-qubit gate demonstrations in a solid-state nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center in diamond, we tested the operation of the resulting protected gates at room temperature and find improvements above an order of magnitude. For a two-qubit CNOT gate, between the nuclear and electron spins, an error per gate of \mbox{$2.7\pm1.9\times10^{-4}$} is measured. Taking into account the increase in the electron coherence time at low temperatures, we predict that a two-qubit error per gate around $3\times10^{-5}$ is achievable. These results, far below the thresholds required by surface and color code error correction, thus present viable building blocks for a new class of fault-tolerant quantum networks.
papers.authors: E. Poem, M. I. Cohen, S. Blum, D. Minin, D. Korn, O. Heifler, A. Hamo, I. Bayn, N. Bar-Gill, R. L. Patel, M. Markham, M. Tordjman

papers.title: Optimizing quantum violation yields facet Bell inequalities
papers.abstract: Nonlocality is revealed through violations of Bell inequalities, whose complete characterization defines the local polytope. For multipartite systems, however, the local polytope becomes rapidly intractable as the number of parties increases. A natural strategy is therefore to optimize Bell inequalities with respect to the ratio of their quantum value to their classical bound. We prove that a nondegenerate local maximum of this ratio gives a facet Bell inequality, and we propose a gradient-based method that searches for such inequalities iteratively. Applied to permutation-invariant scenarios, our method produces tight Bell inequalities with robust quantum violations. Our method enables certification of nonlocality without complete knowledge of the local polytope. More generally, it applies to optimization problems in quantum information involving a classical polytope and a quantum convex set.
papers.authors: Jin-Fu Chen, Mengyao Hu, Jordi Tura

papers.title: ShardQ: Hardware-Aware Circuit Cutting and Recomposition for Quantum Data Encoding
papers.abstract: Quantum data encoding (QDE) loads classical data into quantum states and is a core primitive for quantum machine learning and quantum algorithms, yet executing QDE circuits on connectivity-limited noisy quantum processing units (QPUs) requires a compilation-and-reconstruction pipeline that partitions the circuit across the hardware and recombines the fragment outputs. Circuit cutting and knitting provide such a route, but the benefit depends on selecting a small number of high-value cuts because quasi-probability decomposition (QPD) incurs a sampling overhead that grows as $9^k$ for $k$ cut two-qubit gates. In this study, we introduce shardQ, a hardware-aware cutting and recomposition framework for structured QDE circuits with an address register, a data register, and an enumerable set of cross-register two-qubit gates under a chosen hardware layout. Its cut selector, SparseCut, ranks these candidate gates by hardware graph distance and selects a user-bounded cut set in $O(|\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{cross}}|\log|\mathcal{G}_{\mathrm{cross}}|)$ time, avoiding mixed-integer-programming search in this restricted setting. The remaining truncated circuits are simulated with bond-dimension matrix product states (MPS), while the removed interactions are reconstructed using QPD on classical machines. Hardware measurements are the IBM Heron executions in Table I. Cut-finding, MPS, and overhead studies up to $150+$ qubit layouts are classical simulations or projections, and each such panel is labeled accordingly.
papers.authors: Ziqing Guo, Jan Balewski, Steven Rayan, Kewen Xiao, Ziwen Pan

papers.title: Three-charge black holes from the worldsheet
papers.abstract: We consider the general asymptotically flat, doubly-rotating, three-charge black hole uplifted to a family of NS5-F1-P black brane solutions of Type IIB supergravity. We construct a null-gauged WZW model whose target-space geometry reproduces this background in the NS5 decoupling limit, and show that the gauging parameters precisely satisfy the appropriate consistency conditions on the perturbative string spectrum. Through an analytic continuation and an appropriate limit, this model relates to a recently studied construction describing strings on smooth, horizonless geometries. We further analyze the supersymmetric and extremal three-charge configuration, corresponding to the ten-dimensional uplift of the (NS5-decoupled) BMPV black hole, and show that it requires a novel class of null-gauged WZW models. Our construction provides explicit examples of worldsheet CFTs that capture string dynamics on certain black hole geometries with linear dilaton asymptotics.
papers.authors: Stefano Massai, Enrico Turetta

papers.title: The Weight of $Spin(32)/\mathbb{Z}_2$ Little Strings: T-duality and Hasse Diagrams
papers.abstract: We study the worldvolume theories of stacks of $Spin(32)/\mathbb{Z}_2$ heterotic NS5-branes probing a transverse singularity $\mathfrak{g}$. We revisit and extend the original classification by Blum and Intriligator, and show that the resulting 6d Little String Theories (LSTs) are naturally labeled by affine dominant coweights of the singularity $\mathfrak{g}$. This in turn enables us to efficiently arrange these theories into groupings satisfying all known necessary conditions to be T-dual. Using this formulation, we then study the partial order of those coweights, and extend a recently proposed slice-subtraction algorithm to construct Hasse diagrams for LSTs directly from their six-dimensional generalized quivers, allowing us to probe certain properties of their Higgs branch. Along the way, we exploit these techniques to show that the number of duality orbits at maximal flavor rank is determined by the center of the transverse singularity $\mathfrak{g}$, and provide a simplified proof of a monotonicity theorem for this class of theories. Finally, we show how some of our techniques can be extended to other classes of 6d theories, such as Type-II LSTs and SCFTs.
papers.authors: Hamza Ahmed, Florent Baume, Paul-Konstantin Oehlmann

papers.title: Reduced State Embedding for Quantum Cryptography
papers.abstract: Encoding in a high-dimensional Hilbert space improves noise resilience in quantum information processing. This approach, however, may result in cross-mode coupling and detection complexities, thereby reducing quantum cryptography performance. This fundamental trade-off between correctness and secrecy motivates the search for quantum high-dimensional encoding approaches for cryptography. Here, we introduce state embeddings that use a k-symbol subset within a d-dimensional Hilbert space, tailored to the channel's error structure. We demonstrate the advantage of our scheme in realistic quantum channels, producing a higher secure key rate. We validate our approach using a d=25 quantum key distribution (QKD) experimental data, derive closed-form expressions for the key rate and threshold, and determine the optimum at k=5. These findings advance high-dimensional QKD and pave the way to error-correction and modulation for quantum cryptography.
papers.authors: Amit Kam, Kfir Sulimany, Shai Tsesses, Uzi Pereg

papers.title: A formula for the edge density $\sqrt{n}$-correction for two-dimensional Coulomb systems
papers.abstract: In connection with recent work on smallest gaps, C. Charlier proves that the 1-point function of a suitable planar Coulomb system $\{z_j\}_1^n$, in the determinantal case with respect to an external potential $Q(z)$, admits the expansion, as $n\to\infty$, $$R_n\bigg(z_0+\frac t {\sqrt{2n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)}}\nu(z_0)\bigg)=n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)\frac {\operatorname{erfc} t}2+\sqrt{n\partial\bar{\partial} Q(z_0)}\,C(z_0;t)+\mathcal{O}(\log^6 n).$$ Here $t$ is a real parameter, $z_0$ is a regular boundary point of the (connected) Coulomb droplet and $\nu(z_0)$ is the outwards unit normal; the coefficient $C(z_0;t)$ has an apriori structure depending on a number of parameters. In this note we identify the parameters and obtain a formula for $C(z_0;t)$ in potential theoretic and geometric terms. Our formula holds for a large class of potentials such that the droplet is connected with smooth boundary. Our derivation uses the well known expectation of fluctuations formula.
papers.authors: Yacin Ameur

papers.title: Exact Quantum Circuit Optimization is co-NQP-hard
papers.abstract: As quantum computing resources remain scarce and error rates high, minimizing the resource consumption of quantum circuits is essential for achieving practical quantum advantage. Here we consider the natural problem of, given a circuit $C$, computing a circuit $C'$ that behaves equivalently on a desired subspace, and that minimizes a quantum resource type, expressed as the count or depth of (i) all gates, or (ii) non-Clifford gates, or (iii) superposition gates, or (iv) entanglement gates. We show that, when $C$ is expressed over any gate-set that can implement the H and TOF gates exactly, a standard property of approximately universal gate-sets, each of the above optimization problems is hard for co-NQP, and hence outside the Polynomial Hierarchy, unless the Polynomial Hierarchy collapses. This complements a recent result of Van de Wetering and Amy (arXiv, 2023) which establishes an NP-hardness lower bound when equivalence is over the full state space, and tightens the gap to the corresponding $\text{NP}^\text{NQP}$ upper bound known for cases (i)-(iii) over Clifford+T and (i)-(iv) over H+TOF circuits. Our result also generalizes a result by Tanaka (Int. J. Quantum Inf., 2010) to other gate-sets and quantum resources.
papers.authors: Adam Husted Kjelstr{\o}m, Andreas Pavlogiannis, Jaco van de Pol

papers.title: Covariance and the use of the Schrodinger equation in quantum field theory
papers.abstract: The Schrodinger equation is not covariant. Nevertheless, quantum field theory is often formulated using the Schrodinger equation to describe the time evolution of the system, which is equivalent to using Feynman path integrals. It is well known that scattering theory gives covariant results provided that the interaction vanishes in the asymptotic limit of $t \rightarrow \pm \infty$, but there are other situations of interest that do not satisfy those conditions. As an example, the Aharonov-Bohm effect is derived here using second-quantized field theory to describe all the electrons as well as the electromagnetic field, which allows the effects of retarded vector potentials to be calculated in a straightforward way using the Feynman propagator. The results are in agreement with the usual expression for the Aharonov-Bohm effect when the retardation of the electromagnetic field is negligible, but they predict a fractional phase shift, a lack of covariance, and violations of causality when retardation effects are significant. These results suggest that quantum field theory based on the Schrodinger equation or Feynman path integrals is incomplete in the sense that it cannot give a correct description of all observable phenomena.
papers.authors: J. D. Franson

papers.title: The ribbon category of representations of a crossed module
papers.abstract: The theory of representations of a crossed module is a direct generalization of the theory of representations of groups. For a finite group G, the Drinfeld quantum double of the group G is a Hopf algebra that represents a special case of crossed module of finite groups. Here we study how to extend the construction of the Drinfeld quantum double for any other kind of crossed module of finite groups. This leads to a Hopf algebra D(G,H) that presents similarities with a Drinfeld double. We then study simple subalgebras of D(G,H) and give two isomorphisms for the decomposition into a product of simple subalgebras. We then study the category D(G,H)-mod^Fd of finite dimensional modules over D(G,H), which turns out to be isomorphic to the category of finite dimensional representations of finite crossed modules of groups. These categories being monoidal, we also study links between direct sums of simple objects and tensor products of simple objects and give some results for a Clebsch-Gordan formula. We, in this context, present and develop the character theory for representations of crossed modules of finite groups, and detail the proofs. We then study the category itself, which leads to some ribbon invariants.
papers.authors: Ony Aubril

papers.title: Ultrafast Meissner-Levitated Microrotor
papers.abstract: Levitated mechanical systems offer a unique and flexible platform for the realization of ultralow noise sensors and tests of fundamental physics. Here, we report the demonstration of a levitated microrotor, consisting of a magnetic microsphere levitated by the Meissner effect at 4.2 K. The rotor reaches rotation frequencies above 2.3 MHz (138 million rpm) while exhibiting an exceptionally low damping rate 4.75 $\times$10$^{-7}$ Hz. Exploiting the linear dependence of friction on the gas density, we demonstrate high-accuracy absolute pressure sensing over a wide range at cryogenic temperature. Finally, we detect the thermal torque noise at intermediate pressure by operating the rotor in synchronized mode, resulting in a first preliminary narrowband search for axion-like dark matter. More broadly, the unique combination of high rotational speed, low temperature, and low thermal torque noise establishes a new regime for precision measurements, with direct implications for the detection of extremely weak forces and fields.
papers.authors: Joel K Jose, Andrea Marchese, Marion Cromb, Hendrik Ulbricht, Andrejs Cebers, Ping Koy Lam, Tao Wang, Andrea Vinante

papers.title: Entanglement sharing schemes
papers.abstract: We ask how quantum correlations can be distributed among many subsystems. To address this, we define entanglement sharing schemes (ESS) where certain pairs of subsystems allow entanglement to be recovered via local operations, while other pairs must not. ESS schemes come in two variants, one where the partner system with which entanglement should be prepared is known, and one where it is not. In the case of known partners, we fully characterize the access structures realizable for ESS when using stabilizer states, and construct efficient schemes for threshold access structures, and give a conjecture for the access structures realizable with general states. In the unknown partner case, we again give a complete characterization in the stabilizer setting, additionally give a complete characterization of the case where there are no restrictions on unauthorized pairs, and we prove a set of necessary conditions on general schemes which we conjecture are also sufficient. Finally, we give an application of the theory of entanglement sharing to resolve an open problem related to the distribution of entanglement in response to time-sensitive requests in quantum networks.
papers.authors: Zahra Khanian, Dongjin Lee, Debbie Leung, Zhi Li, Alex May, Takato Mori, Stanley Miao, Farzin Salek, Jinmin Yi, Beni Yoshida

papers.title: Sublinear Time Quantum Sensitivity Sampling
papers.abstract: We present a unified quantum sensitivity sampling framework that streamlines coreset construction for many classical approximation problems, significantly speeding up clustering, regression, and low-rank approximation. We assume $n,d\geq\mathrm{poly}(k/\epsilon)$ and, for regression, $n\geq\mathrm{poly}(d)$: - $k$-median/$k$-means: For $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$, we build an $\epsilon$-coreset of input points of size $\tilde O(k^{4/3}\epsilon^{-2})$ (resp. $\tilde O(k^{3/2}\epsilon^{-2})$) in time $\tilde O(\epsilon^{-1}n^{0.5}dk^{1.67})$ (resp. $\tilde O(\epsilon^{-1}n^{0.5}dk^{1.75})$). Our better $d$- and linear $1/\epsilon$-dependence improve on [Xue, Chen, Li and Jiang, ICML'23] for $d\geq\Omega(k^{7/3})$ (resp. $\Omega(k^{2.5})$). - $\ell_p$ regression: For $\min_x\|Ax-b\|_p$, $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$, we build an $\epsilon$-coreset of size $\tilde O_p(d^{\max\{1,p/2\}}\epsilon^{-2})$ in time $\tilde O_p(n^{0.5}d^{1.5}\epsilon^{-1})$ for $p\leq 2$ and $\tilde O_p(n^{0.5}d^{p/4+1}(\epsilon^{-1}+d^{0.5}))$ for $p>2$, matching [Liu and Ji, ICML'26] for $p\leq 2$ and improving on the prior best quantum sampling approach [Apers and Gribling, SICOMP'26] for all $p>2$. - Low-rank approximation: We give the first quantum sublinear-time algorithm for Frobenius-norm rank-$k$ approximation of $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times n}$ free of data-dependent parameters, running in $\tilde O(n^{0.5}dk^{0.5}\epsilon^{-0.5})$ time with factored output (plus $\tilde O(nk^2\epsilon^{-2})$ to materialize them). We also give sublinear algorithms for kernel and tensor variants. - Lower bound: For generic sensitivity sampling with total sensitivity $S$, any quantum algorithm outputting an $\epsilon$-coreset of size $o(\sqrt{nS})$ needs $\Omega(\sqrt{nS})$ queries, so our query complexity is optimal up to $\mathrm{poly}(\epsilon^{-1},\log n)$ and VC-dimension factors.
papers.authors: Zhao Song, David P. Woodruff, Lichen Zhang

papers.title: Finite dimensional approximations for Hilbert space operators and applications in Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract: In this work, we develop a unified framework for quasidiagonal and F\o lner-type approximations of linear operators on Hilbert spaces. These approximations (originally formulated for bounded operators and operator algebras) involve sequences of non-zero finite rank orthogonal projections that asymptotically commute with the operator -- either in norm (quasidiagonal) or in mean (F\o lner). Such structures guarantee spectral approximation results in terms of their finite sections. We extend this theory to unbounded, densely defined closable operators, establishing a generalization of Halmos' classical result: every closable quasidiagonal operator is a compact perturbation of a closable block-diagonal operator on the same domain. Likewise, we introduce sparse F\o lner sequences and establish an interplay between quasidiagonal approximations and the existence of sparse F\o lner sequences. The theoretical developments are illustrated with explicit examples using different types of weighted shifts and applied to quantum mechanical models, including a detailed treatment of the Weyl algebra and its Schr\"odinger representation.
papers.authors: Eva A. Gallardo-Guti\'errez, Fernando Lled\'o, Laura S\'aenz

papers.title: Atom Interferometer Phase Shear and Spacetime Sectional Curvature
papers.abstract: Atom interferometry is a natural laboratory for precision tests of general relativity, but there are no known simple relationships between atom interferometer phase and geometric properties of spacetime. Here we show that a different atom interferometer observable, the phase shear, can be expressed directly as the integrated sectional curvature over a spacetime surface enclosed by the interferometer arms and final beamsplitter, which follows from a generalized Gauss-Bonnet theorem. This interface of quantum mechanics, relativity, and geometry is manifestly coordinate-free and representation-free and can provide a useful computational tool for predicting atom interferometer properties in arbitrary background spacetimes.
papers.authors: Hunter Swan, Jason M. Hogan

papers.title: Smallest gaps of the two-dimensional Coulomb gas
papers.abstract: We consider the two-dimensional Coulomb gas with a general potential at the determinantal temperature, or equivalently, the eigenvalues of random normal matrices. We prove that the smallest gaps between particles are typically of order $n^{-3/4}$, and that the associated joint point process of gap locations and gap sizes, after rescaling the gaps by $n^{3/4}$, converges to a Poisson point process. As a consequence, we show that the $k$-th smallest rescaled gap has a limiting density proportional to $x^{4k-1}e^{-\frac{\mathcal{J}}{4}x^{4}}$, where $\mathcal{J}=\pi^{2}\int \rho(z)^{3}d^{2}z$ and $\rho$ is the density of the equilibrium measure. This generalizes a result of Shi and Jiang beyond the quadratic potential.
papers.authors: Christophe Charlier

papers.title: On the consistency of non-commutative geometry inspired Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m black hole solution
papers.abstract: We revisit the non-commutative geometry inspired Reissner-Nordstr\"{o}m black hole solution obtained by smearing the point sources with a Gaussian distribution. We show that while the form of the metric function and the physical properties derived from that remain valid, not all the components of Einstein equations are satisfied: the angular components fail by exactly the Lorentz force density exerted by the electric field on the smeared charge, which the standard electromagnetic energy-momentum tensor leaves unbalanced. We construct an improved energy-momentum tensor that consistently satisfies Einstein equations. It is the unique conserved completion: the standard Maxwell tensor supplemented by an interaction stress supported on the smeared source. The improved tensor leads to a different prediction for the region where the strong energy condition is violated. For certain choice of parameters, our proposal predicts the violation of the energy condition outside the Cauchy horizon, which might be relevant for the stability of the inner horizon and strong cosmic censorship.
papers.authors: Gokhan Alkac, Murat Mesta, Gonul Unal

papers.title: Affine Equivalence in the Clifford Hierarchy
papers.abstract: In this paper we prove a collection of results on the structure of permutations in the Clifford Hierarchy. First, we leverage results from the cryptography literature on affine equivalence classes of 4-bit permutations which we use to find all 4-qubit permutations in the Clifford Hierarchy. We then use the classification of 4-qubit permutations and previous results on the structure of diagonal gates in the Clifford Hierarchy to prove that all 4-qubit gates in the third level of the Clifford Hierarchy are semi-Clifford. We then leverage results from \cite{He2024} to prove that all 5-qubit gates in the third level of the Clifford Hierarchy are semi-Clifford. We introduce the formalism of cycle structures to permutations in the Clifford Hierarchy and prove a general structure theorem about them, and classify many small cycle structures up to affine equivalence. Interestingly, this classification is independent of the number of qubits. Additionally, we show that all 1-wire-mismatch permutations are in the Clifford Hierarchy.
papers.authors: Jonas T. Anderson, Andrew Connelly, Mason Lovejoy-Johnson

papers.title: Pilot-waves and copilot-particles: A nonstochastic approach to objective wavefunction collapse
papers.abstract: We seek an extension to Schrodinger's equation that incorporates the macroscopic measurement-induced wavefunction collapse phenomenon. We find that a suitable hybrid between two leading approaches, the Bohm-de Broglie pilot-wave and objective collapse theories, accomplishes this goal in a way that is consistent with Born's rule. Our theory posits that the Bohmian particle is guided by the wavefunction and, conversely, the wavefunction gradually localizes towards the particle's position. As long as the particle can visit any state, as in a typical microscopic system, the localization effect does not favor any particular quantum state and, on average, the usual Schrodinger-like time evolution results. However, when the wavefunction develops spatially well-separated lobes, as would happen during a macroscopic measurement, the Bohmian particle can remain trapped in one lobe, which causes the wavefunction to eventually localizes. This proposed loss of ergodicity mechanism recasts one of the foundational postulate of quantum mechanics as a emergent feature and has important implications regarding the feasibility of large-scale quantum computing.
papers.authors: Axel van de Walle

papers.title: Observation of gyroscopic coupling in a non-spinning levitated ferromagnet
papers.abstract: A non-spinning permanent ferromagnet is predicted to behave as a gyroscope at sufficiently low frequencies, which can be seen as a manifestation of gyromagnetism. This yet unexplored regime, conjectured for the first time by Maxwell in 1861, has recently been proposed for ultrasensitive magnetometry and for atomic-like quantum stabilization of a levitated nanomagnet in a static field. Here, we observe signatures of gyroscopic effects in the rotational dynamics of a non-spinning permanent ferromagnet levitated in a superconducting trap. Specifically, we detect spin-rotation coupling between different librational modes, leading to elliptical trajectories, in good agreement with theoretical predictions. From our measurements, we can infer both the intrinsic angular momentum of the levitated magnet and its gyromagnetic $g$-factor.
papers.authors: F. Ahrens, A. Vinante

papers.title: Conserved quantities of distinguished curves on conformal sphere
papers.abstract: We give conserved quantities of two generalizations of conformal circles on the conformal sphere. One generalization concerns curves carrying a distinguished parallel tractor along them, which can be used to construct the conserved quantities. The other is the class of curves satisfying the conformal Mercator equation, the conserved quantities of which are computed using Lagrangian formalism. The two generalizations are not disjoint, and our main result is the relation between their conserved quantities. Explicit examples are also presented.
papers.authors: Prim Plansangkate, Lenka Zalabov\'a

papers.title: Effect of ultralight dark matter on compact binary mergers
papers.abstract: The growing catalogue of gravitational wave events enables a statistical analysis of compact binary mergers, typically quantified by the binary merger rate density. This quantity can be influenced by ambient factors, following which, in this work we have investigated the impact of dark matter environment on the merger statistics. We construct a baseline astrophysical model of eccentric and quasi-circular compact binary mergers and extend it by incorporating a model of ultra light dark matter, which affects the orbital evolution of binaries through accretion and dynamical friction. Our analysis of the merged population of binary progenitors demonstrates that, compared to the baseline model, ULDM can potentially alter the merger statistics for ambient non-zero densities, with the best agreement with GWTC-3 obtained for $\rho_0\sim10^6$ GeV/cm$^3$ and eccentricity $\sim0.5$. A comparison with the gravitational wave data from the GWTC-3 catalogue provides crucial insight into potential observational signatures of the ULDM in merger events, leading to possible constraints on the existence and density of dark matter distribution in galaxies.
papers.authors: Kabir Chakravarti, Soham Acharya, Sumanta Chakraborty, Sudipta Sarkar

papers.title: Certified Lipschitz Bounds for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Decision Models
papers.abstract: We study certified upper bounds on Lipschitz constants for hybrid quantum-classical decision models, which combine classical neural-network layers with parameterized quantum circuits. We pair an SDP-based certificate for classical layers with an exact spectral characterization for probability-output quantum models. For hybrid architectures, these componentwise estimates are connected through the encoding maps to obtain a certified composition bound for the complete model. The resulting bounds support sensitivity analyses relevant to robustness, stability, generalization, and fairness.
papers.authors: Sajjad Hashemian, Mohammad Saeed Arvenaghi

papers.title: Self-correcting qubit in a strongly driven LC resonator
papers.abstract: We propose a device to realize quantum error correction by dissipation. The device generates Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) states as steady states in a single driven LC resonator. The resonator should have impedance above $h/2e^2\approx 12.9\,{\rm k}\Omega$, and should be driven across a Josephson junction with a high-amplitude voltage tone at frequency near-commensurate with the resonator frequency. In this regime, we show that GKP states emerge as steady-states of the resonator; these states encode a qubit protected against phase-space local noise. Low-lying excitations preserve the quantum information and increase the energy proportionally to a measure of the error degree. Thus, quantum error correction of both bit and phase errors can be achieved with dissipative cooling. Our calculations indicate an achievable coherence time of $ 1000 \times$ the resonator photon lifetime at operating temperatures above $100 \, {\rm mK}$. Beyond steady-state quantum error correction, the device supports protected single-qubit Clifford gates and readout with exponential accuracy corrected by the same dissipative mechanism, as well as magic-state preparation above the distillation threshold.
papers.authors: Max Geier, Frederik Nathan

papers.title: Lazy Qubit Reordering for Accelerating Parallel State-Vector-based Quantum Circuit Simulation
papers.abstract: This article proposes two quantum operation scheduling methods for accelerating parallel state-vector-based quantum circuit simulation using multiple graphics processing units (GPUs). The proposed methods reduce all-to-all communication caused by qubit reordering, which can dominate the overhead of parallel simulation. Our out-of-order approach eliminates redundant reorderings by introducing intentional delays in reordering communications such that multiple reorderings can be aggregated into a single reordering. The delays are carefully introduced based on the principles of time-space tiling, or a cache optimization technique for classical computers, which we use to arrange the execution order of quantum operations. Moreover, we develop these methods tailored for two primary procedures in variational quantum eigensolver simulation: quantum state update (QSU) and expectation value computation (EVC). Our QSU simulation takes an advantage of the hierarchical interconnection of GPU systems to avoid slow inter-node communication. On the other hand, our EVC simulation reduces the number of reorderings by diagonalization of Pauli strings. Experimental validation on 32-GPU executions demonstrates acceleration in QSU and EVC$\unicode{x2014}$up to 54$\times$ and 1,657$\times$, respectively$\unicode{x2014}$compared to an inorder-based method. We believe that our out-of-order approach is useful for accelerating large-scale quantum circuit simulations, including QSU and/or EVC that operate qubits in a regular manner.
papers.authors: Yusuke Teranishi, Shoma Hiraoka, Wataru Mizukami, Masao Okita, Fumihiko Ino

papers.title: Sample-Efficient Quantum State Tomography for Structured Quantum States in One Dimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, we answer this fundamental question affirmatively by using a class of informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (IC-POVMs), including symmetric IC-POVMs (SIC-POVMs) and spherical $t$-designs, focusing on sample complexity while not accounting for the implementation complexity of the measurement settings. For SIC-POVMs and spherical 2-designs, we show that the number of state copies to guarantee bounded recovery error of an MPO state with a constrained least-squares estimator depends on the probability distribution of the MPO under the POVM but scales only linearly with $n$ when the distribution is approximately uniform. For general spherical $t$-designs with a sufficiently large $t$, we prove that only a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is sufficient for a guaranteed recovery of any state represented by an MPO. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound based on the Cramer-Rao bound, showing that, for strictly positive definite MPO states and unbiased estimators, a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is also necessary, although the upper and lower bounds do not yet match in their dependence on the target accuracy. Furthermore, we propose a spectral method and a projected gradient descent (PGD) algorithm to solve the constrained least-squares problem, both equipped with rigorous recovery error guarantees.
papers.authors: Zhen Qin, Casey Jameson, Alireza Goldar, Michael B. Wakin, Zhexuan Gong, Zhihui Zhu

papers.title: Gapped and gapless quantum spin liquids on the ruby lattice
papers.abstract: The ruby lattice has been the subject of much interest recently due to its realization in Rydberg atom arrays, where its rich variety of frustrated interactions gives rise to topologically ordered quantum spin liquids. Similarly, numerical studies of ruby-lattice spin models, with both isotropic and anisotropic interactions, have provided evidence of gapped and gapless spin-liquid ground states with different low-energy gauge structures. Motivated by these findings, we perform a projective symmetry group (PSG) classification of U(1) and $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ fermionic spinon mean-field theories$\unicode{x2014}$respecting space-group and time-reversal symmetries$\unicode{x2014}$for $S=1/2$ spins. We obtain a total of 50 U(1) and 64 $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ PSGs, and upon restricting their realization via mean-field $\textit{Ans\"atze}$ with up to second-nearest-neighbor singlet amplitudes (relevant to the models studied here), only 8 U(1) and 18 $\mathbb{Z}_{2}$ distinct states are obtained. We present the singlet fields for all $\textit{Ans\"atze}$ up to third-nearest-neighboring bonds and discuss their spinon dispersions as well as their dynamical spin structure factors. Building on this information, we also obtain the phase diagram of the Heisenberg model in the presence of first- ($J_{1}$), second- ($J_{1}'$), and third- ($J_{2}$) neighbor antiferromagnetic couplings within a self-consistent mean-field approximation.
papers.authors: Atanu Maity, Rhine Samajdar, Yasir Iqbal

papers.title: The principle of relativity in classical nonholonomic mechanics and $G$-Chaplygin systems with affine time-dependent constraints
papers.abstract: We study the principle of relativity in classical time-dependent nonholonomic Lagrangian mechanics from the perspective of moving global reference frames. We also introduce time-dependent $G$-Chaplygin systems with affine constraints, which are natural objects for the invariant formulation of nonholonomic systems with symmetries. As far as the author is aware, the Hamiltonization problem for time-dependent constraints has not yet been studied. As a first step in this direction, we consider a rolling without sliding of a balanced disc of radius $r$ over a vertical circle of a given variable radius $R(t)$. We modify the Chaplygin multiplier method and prove that the reduced system becomes Hamiltonian with respect to the new time.
papers.authors: Bozidar Jovanovic

papers.title: Scattering and bound observables for spinning particles in Kerr spacetime with generic spin orientations
papers.abstract: We derive the radial action of a spinning probe particle in Kerr spacetime from the worldline formalism in the first-order form, focusing on linear in spin effects. We then develop a novel covariant Dirac bracket formalism to compute the impulse and the spin kick directly from the radial action, generalizing some conjectural results in the literature and providing ready-to-use expressions for amplitude calculations with generic spin orientations. This allows, for the first time, to find new covariant expressions for scattering observables in the probe limit up to $\mathcal{O}(G^6 s_1 s_2^4)$. Finally, we use the action-angle representation to compute the fundamental frequencies for generic bound orbits, including the intrinsic spin precession, the periastron advance and the precession of the orbital plane.
papers.authors: Riccardo Gonzo, Canxin Shi

papers.title: Thermal Krylov complexity and entropy of inflationary modes with different comoving-wavenumber dependences
papers.abstract: We study thermal Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy for primordial scalar modes in three inflationary models with different comoving-wavenumber dependences. These models are canonical single-field inflation, a non-trivial sound speed model, and a modified dispersion relation model. We construct a purified two-mode thermal state and first study its unitary Krylov evolution in an ideal closed system. In the parameter range considered here, the sound-speed correction increases the mean values and oscillation amplitudes of the Krylov quantities. The modified dispersion relation produces a stage-dependent oscillatory structure. We then introduce an independent effective open-system parametrization. The normalized Krylov distribution is controlled by a geometric ratio that combines thermal occupation, coherent spreading, and effective attenuation. We derive explicit expressions for Krylov complexity and Krylov entropy. We also obtain their low- and high-temperature limits. The sound-speed correction enhances the geometric ratio in the adopted parameter range. For the modified dispersion relation, coherent spreading and effective attenuation compete. These results show how thermal occupation and modified mode frequencies control Krylov-space spreading in the three inflationary models.
papers.authors: Tao Li, Lei-Hua Liu

papers.title: Deep Tensor Network
papers.abstract: The Deep Tensor Network is a family of sequence operators built from contractions of queries, keys, and values. Tensor Attention mixes tokens through the Gram operators $Q(K^\top K)Q^\top$ and $K(Q^\top Q)K^\top$; Tensor Interaction mixes channels through operators derived from $C=Q^\top K$. Associativity lets us evaluate these products exactly without forming $n\times n$ token matrices. For query/key width $d$ and value width $d_v$, the Gram constructions use $O(d^2+dd_v)$ work and summary state per causal token, or $O(d^2)$ when $d_v=O(d)$. We derive prefix recurrences and distinguish trace, diagonal, and row normalization, including the conditions under which the weights are nonnegative and row-stochastic. The unmasked token operators are positive semidefinite with rank at most $d$, but their entries can be negative. We also give exact evaluations and costs for Hadamard and matrix-exponential variants.
papers.authors: Yifan Zhang

papers.title: Kerr-athermal baths enhance cooling in quantum refrigerators
papers.abstract: We study a three-qubit quantum refrigerator, with a three-body interaction enabling cooling of the target qubit, coupled to harmonic oscillator baths prepared in stationary Kerr-athermal states. The reservoir occupation probabilities are specified by a Kerr-type preparation Hamiltonian, while the bath dynamics during operation are harmonic. We show that these reservoirs lower the steady-state temperature of the cold qubit relative to the thermal-bath reference. The improvement of steady-state cooling is distinct from that of the minimum transient temperature, which is not universally enhanced. In a parameter regime where the thermal reference exhibits only transient cold-qubit cooling, the engineered Kerr-athermal baths can produce a steady-state temperature below the initial value. We also investigate the dependence of the steady-state temperature and minimum attainable temperatures on the anharmonicity in the bath state. Analysis of bath-currents reveals lower steady-state temperatures with nearly unchanged coefficients of performance, revealing that reservoir engineering leads to cold-qubit cooling.
papers.authors: Tanaya Ray, Sayan Mondal, Aparajita Bhattacharyya, Ahana Ghoshal, Debraj Rakshit, Ujjwal Sen

papers.title: The Geometric Deformation of Curved $L_\infty$ Algebras and Lie Algebroids
papers.abstract: While $L_\infty$ algebras are fundamental structures in differential geometry and mathematical physics, the geometric information encoded in such structures is often implicit. We address the following question: What constitutes a geometrically meaningful deformation of an $L_\infty$ algebra arising from vector bundles, and how can such deformations classify new geometric invariants? Inspired by nonabelian extension theory of Lie algebras, we define geometric deformations of curved $L_\infty$ algebras constructed from a vector bundle $V\to M$, and demonstrate that such deformations uniquely correspond to Lie algebroid structures on $V$. Explicit computations reveal that a representative of the first Atiyah-Chern class is exact in the total Weil complex, with its primitive representing the modular class in Lie algebroid cohomology. In the case of action Lie algebroids, the leading-order Atiyah-Chern classes correspond to the equivariant Chern characters. Applications to BV theories show that the geometric deformations naturally generate Poisson sigma models. These results provide a coherent framework for deriving field theories from geometric deformations of $L_\infty$ algebras.
papers.authors: Xiaoyi Cui

papers.title: Measuring the Hubble Constant Using Strongly Lensed Gravitational Wave Signals
papers.abstract: The measurement of the Hubble constant $H_0$ plays an important role in the study of cosmology. In this letter, we propose a new method to constrain the Hubble constant using the strongly lensed gravitational wave (GW) signals. By reparameterizing the waveform, we find that the lensed waveform is sensitive to the $H_0$. Assuming the scenario that no electromagnetic counterpart of the GW source can be identified, our method can still give meaningful constraints on the $H_0$ with the information of the lens redshift. We then apply Fisher information matrix and Markov Chain Monte Carlo to evaluate the potential of this method. For the space-based GW detector, TianQin, the $H_0$ can be constrained within a relative error of $\sim$ 0.3-2\%, using a single strongly lensed GW event. Precision varies according to different levels of electromagnetic information.
papers.authors: Shun-Jia Huang, Yi-Ming Hu, Xian Chen, Jian-dong Zhang, En-Kun Li, Zucheng Gao, Xin-Yi Lin

papers.title: On Noetherianity of tensor modules and homology of subalgebras of vector fields
papers.abstract: We show that finite tensor products $\otimes_{i=1}^{r}\mathcal{T}_{\lambda}$ of modules of tensor fields are Noetherian modules over any Lie subalgebra of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on $\mathbb{R}^n$. Moreover, the Hilbert series of their graded submodules are rational functions whose denominators are products of factors of the form $(1-t^m)$. As a corollary, we prove the conjecture of I.\,M. Gelfand, announced at the ICM in Nice in 1970, on the finite-dimensionality of the continuous cohomology of graded Lie subalgebras of finite codimension in the Lie algebra of formal vector fields $\mathcal{W}_n$. We also prove that tensor products of modules of densities are Noetherian over the Witt Lie algebra of polynomial vector fields on the punctured line. Moreover, for a weight $\lambda\neq0,1$ every nonzero submodule of the symmetric power $S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$ contains $\Delta^{2d}S^r(\mathcal{T}_\lambda)$, where $\Delta$ is the Vandermonde determinant. As a consequence, we show that a conjecture of Etingof implies the conjecture of Petukhov and Sierra on the simplicity of the quotients $U(\vir)/(C-c)$ of the enveloping algebra of the Virasoro algebra.
papers.authors: Boris Feigin, Alexei Kanel-Belov, Anton Khoroshkin

papers.title: The Brown measure of a sum of two free nonselfadjoint random variables, one of which is R-diagonal
papers.abstract: Suppose that $X_1$ and $X_2$ are two $*$-free, possibly unbounded, random variables with Brown measures $\mu_{X_1}$ and $\mu_{X_2}$ respectively. Using properties of classic free additive convolution, we develop a method for calculating $\mu_{X_1+X_2}$ when $X_2$ is $R$-diagonal. This method determines a density relative to Lebesgue measure on an open set whose closure equals the support of $\mu_{X_{1}+X_{2}}$. We prove that $\mu_{X_1+X_2}$ has no singular continuous part, that its density is strictly positive on this open set, and we determine the masses of its atoms. Explicit calculations are possible in several important cases. As an application, we combine our Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula with known subordination convergence results to calculate the limiting logarithmic potentials of free multiplicative random walks. We identify the limit with the Fuglede--Kadison determinant formula for free multiplicative Brownian motion previously proved by some PDE methods.
papers.authors: Hari Bercovici, Yu Kitagawa, Ping Zhong

papers.title: Scaling at quantum phase transitions above the upper critical dimension
papers.abstract: The hyperscaling relation and standard finite-size scaling (FSS) are known to break down above the upper critical dimension due to dangerous irrelevant variables. We establish a coherent formalism for FSS at quantum phase transitions above the upper critical dimension following the recently introduced Q-FSS formalism for thermal phase transitions. Contrary to long-standing belief, the correlation sector is affected by dangerous irrelevant variables. The presented formalism recovers a generalized hyperscaling relation and FSS form. Using this new FSS formalism, we determine the full set of critical exponents for the long-range transverse-field Ising chain in all criticality regimes ranging from the nearest-neighbor to the long-range mean field regime. For the same model, we also explicitly confirm the effect of dangerous irrelevant variables on the characteristic length scale.
papers.authors: A. Langheld, J. A. Koziol, P. Adelhardt, S. C. Kapfer, K. P. Schmidt

papers.title: Plethora of cluster structures on $GL_n$
papers.abstract: We continue the study of multiple cluster structures in the rings of regular functions on $GL_n$, $SL_n$ and $\operatorname{Mat}_n$ that are compatible with Poisson-Lie and Poisson-homogeneous structures. According to our initial conjecture, each class in the Belavin-Drinfeld classification of Poisson--Lie structures on a semisimple complex group $\mathcal G$ corresponds to a cluster structure in $\mathcal O(\mathcal G)$. Here we prove this conjecture for a large subset of Belavin-Drinfeld (BD) data of $A_n$ type, which includes all the previously known examples. Namely, we subdivide all possible $A_n$ type BD data into oriented and non-oriented kinds. In the oriented case, we single out BD data satisfying a certain combinatorial condition that we call aperiodicity and prove that for any BD data of this kind there exists a regular cluster structure compatible with the corresponding Poisson-Lie bracket. In fact, we extend the aperiodicity condition to pairs of oriented BD data and prove a more general result that establishes an existence of a regular cluster structure on $SL_n$ compatible with a Poisson bracket homogeneous with respect to the right and left action of two copies of $SL_n$ equipped with two different Poisson-Lie brackets. If the aperiodicity condition is not satisfied, a compatible cluster structure has to be replaced with a generalized cluster structure. We will address this situation in future publications.
papers.authors: Misha Gekhtman, Michael Shapiro, Alek Vainshtein

papers.title: On some formality criteria for DG-Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We give some formality criteria for a differential graded Lie algebra to be formal. For instance, we show that a DG-Lie algebra L is formal if and only if the natural spectral sequence computing the Chevalley-Eilenberg cohomology H(L,L) degenerates at second page.
papers.authors: Marco Manetti

papers.title: Emerging of massive gauge particles in inhomogeneous local gauge transformations
papers.abstract: A generalized theory of gauge transformations is presented on the basis of the covariant Hamiltonian formalism of field theory, for which the covariant canonical field equations are equivalent to the Euler-Lagrange field equations. Similar to the canonical transformation theory of point dynamics, the canonical transformation rules for fields are derived from generating functions. Thus---in contrast to the usual Lagrangian description---the covariant canonical transformation formalism automatically ensures the mappings to preserve the action principle, and hence to be {\em physical}. On that basis, we work out the theory of inhomogeneous local gauge transformations that generalizes the conventional local SU(N) gauge transformation theory. It is shown that massive gauge bosons naturally emerge in this description, which thus could supersede the Higgs mechanism.
papers.authors: J\"urgen Struckmeier

papers.title: Energy of test objects on black hole spacetimes: A brief review
papers.abstract: In this paper, we review the issue of defining energy for test particles on a background stationary spacetime. We revisit the different notions of energy as defined by different observers. As is well known, the existence of a time-like isometry allows for the notion of total conserved energy to be well defined. We use this well known quantity to show that a gravitational potential energy can be consistently defined. As examples, we study the case of the exterior regions of an asymptotically flat black hole and of the $\Lambda>0$ Schwarzschild de Sitter case, where an asymptotic region is not available. We then consider the situation in which the test particle is absorbed by the black hole, and analyze the energetics in detail. In particular, we show that the notion of horizon energy as defined by the isolated horizons formalism provides a satisfactory notion of energy compatible with the particle's total conserved energy. With these choices, there is a global conservation of energy. Finally, we comment on a recent proposal to define energy of the black hole as seen by a nearby observer at rest, for which this feature is lost.
papers.authors: Alejandro Corichi

papers.title: Novikov-Magnus Master Equation for Driven Quantum Systems under Classical Correlated Noise
papers.abstract: We introduce a modular framework for deriving time-local quantum master equations for driven systems subject to temporally correlated classical noise. The construction combines the Donsker-Furutsu-Novikov relation with the Magnus expansion: Functional response closes the noise average, while nested commutators retain the noncommuting chronological action of noise-induced perturbations along the controlled quantum trajectory. For zero-mean Gaussian noise, we derive the resulting Novikov-Magnus quantum master equation through fourth order in the noise strength. The same response hierarchy suggests a natural extension beyond Gaussian noise, with connected higher-order noise correlations weighting higher functional derivatives of the stochastic map. For a driven qubit under Ornstein-Uhlenbeck and band-limited $1/f$ noise, the second- and fourth-order maps remain CPTP throughout the perturbative regime and accurately reproduce stochastic simulations. Their diamond-norm errors are comparable to those of the cumulant-based pseudo-Lindblad master equation, with a modest fourth-order improvement for Ornstein-Uhlenbeck noise.
papers.authors: Nada Khogeer, Jerison Parra, Caroline Desgranges, Hugo Ribeiro

papers.title: Trajectory-Dependent Decoherence and Leakage During Shuttling of Multi-Spin Qubits
papers.abstract: Logical qubits encoded in collective states of multiple spins are promising building blocks for large-scale semiconductor quantum processors. As novel fault-tolerant architectures increasingly rely on qubit shuttling, understanding decoherence of the shuttled multi-spin qubits becomes crucial. We analyze fidelity and leakage of the logical qubits dephased by the spatio-temporally correlated $1/f$ noise, considering two-, three-, and four-spin encodings. We study different shuttling protocols and establish that for all encodings generally, parallel shuttling provides the best protection against decoherence at short distances, whereas sequential shuttling outperforms others for long-range transport (although the exact boundaries depend on the specific device parameters). We explain this common behavior in terms of the dephasing factors of pairs of the shuttled spins; we provide explicit expressions for fidelities and leakage, thus enabling experimentalists to predict performance of the multi-spin qubits from only several independently measured pairwise dephasing factors. Our results establish a connection between shuttling trajectories, noise correlations, and qubit decoherence, and provide guidance for achieving noise-resilient shuttling in scalable semiconductor quantum processors.
papers.authors: Yu-Ning Zhang, Aleksandr S. Mokeev, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, David P. DiVincenzo, Viatcheslav V. Dobrovitski

papers.title: Existence of extremal solutions in the 1d conformal bootstrap
papers.abstract: Extremal solutions and functionals play an important role in the conformal bootstrap. These are the solutions that saturate unitarity bounds, and the dual functionals that encode the optimal bounds. While they have fundamental theoretical implications, their existence has not been rigorously established. This is particularly subtle in the setting of the full infinite-dimensional bootstrap, i.e. the limit of zero numerical truncation. In this article, we prove that extremal solutions exist for OPE maximisation problems in 1d CFT. These are a large class of generically interacting, unitary, exact solutions of the crossing equation that maximise an OPE coefficient. We also prove that these problems have 'zero duality gap', meaning there exist functionals arbitrarily close to extremality. Our approach is to formulate the bootstrap as a convex optimisation problem in a Hilbert space and apply the Fenchel-Rockafellar theorem.
papers.authors: Filip Her\v{c}ek, Nat Levine

papers.title: Emergence and polymer physics of the center-vortex network: Confronting SU(4) lattice Yang-Mills theory
papers.abstract: The geometric organization and statistical properties of center-vortex networks provide a window into the infrared dynamics underlying confinement in Yang-Mills theory. Motivated by this connection, we investigate new consequences of a previously proposed confinement mechanism based on physically equivalent elementary Cartan fluxes. We show that, in the percolating phase, these fluxes dynamically reorganize into center-charge sectors whose dominant vortex tensions satisfy a Casimir scaling law, similar to that observed for confining string tensions. We then confront this result with the first nontrivial Yang-Mills case: the doubly charged vortex chains recently observed in SU(4) lattice simulations. To extract the parameters needed to connect the lattice ensemble with the effective description, we characterize how center-vortex chains grow and bend in SU(3) and SU(4) using polymer-inspired techniques not previously applied to center vortices. We find good quantitative agreement for the SU(4) doubly charged sector, providing further evidence for the proposed mechanism.
papers.authors: Luis E. Oxman, Jackson A. Mickley, Derek B. Leinweber

papers.title: A Quantum Mechanical Description of Active Matter
papers.abstract: The natural environments habitable to life are inseparable from dissipative and entropic forces, which mandate active matter to operate on constant fluxes of energy and momentum to survive and propagate through spacetime. In contrast to fundamental particles which are characterized by energy and momentum, we postulate that energy expenditure rate and momentum generation rate are the fundamental dynamical quantities driving this evolution of swimming active matter and accordingly construct the corresponding Lagrangian and Hamiltonian of motion of the active matter. Furthermore, living systems broadly employ periodic, non-repeating motion for both locomotion and various biological functions, with meaningful information stored in the periods of these functions. Consequently, analyzing these dynamics in the Fourier space lands us at the familiar tools of the operator based, quantum mechanics. This is accomplished by introducing a complex field to describe the evolving probability distribution of a single unit, as well as the population density of mutually non-interacting active particles under the constraint of scarce resources. The resulting single-unit wavefunction evolves analogously to the Dirac equation with minimal coupling, wherein gauge symmetry reflects the generality of the governing equations across arbitrary resource landscapes. Additionally, we present a Schr\"odinger-like equation where the effective potential term represents the environmentally mandated, non-motile base metabolic rate. Finally, we formalize the bidirectional coupling between active swimmers and the surrounding fluid via a multipole expansion of the active force with an emphasis on force monopoles and dipoles, where each pole corresponds to a distinct mode of active motility.
papers.authors: Ghansham Chandel, Siddhartha Das

papers.title: Particle production from noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole
papers.abstract: By considering a massless Klein-Gordon field and the moving mirror model, we calculate particle production for a noncommutative-inspired Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole sourced by smeared distributions of mass and charge. We show that noncommutative truncated trajectories diminish the emission spectrum at large frequencies, due to noncommutative effects on the external surface gravity of the black hole, in sharp contrast with the spectrum of a classical Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole.
papers.authors: Alberto Maya, Marco Maceda

papers.title: Classical control of quantum-state relaxation in confined molecular hydrogen
papers.abstract: Quantum-state conversion between the ortho and para nuclear-spin states of H$_2$ is forbidden in the isolated molecule but these states can become connected through interactions with a surrounding environment. How that same environment governs the dynamics of the newly connected states remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate this problem using H$_2$ confined in crystalline molecular solids, where the host environment selectively enables conversion between a pair of otherwise disconnected ortho-H$_2$ and para-H$_2$ states. Rotationally resolved infrared spectroscopy directly determines the state-specific conversion dynamics in crystalline CO$_2$ and N$_2$O at 10 K, revealing that increasing H$_2$ concentration suppresses nuclear-spin conversion by nearly an order of magnitude, reaching complete suppression by 20% H$_2$ loading. Molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo simulations identify two complementary origins of this concentration dependence: changes in the thermally populated phonon modes available to mediate relaxation, and strain-driven H$_2$ clustering that progressively removes molecules from the host crystal field responsible for enabling conversion. The resulting picture connects a classical collective response of the host to microscopic quantum-state dynamics: H$_2$ loading generates strain that reorganizes the local molecular environment, thereby modifying both the phonon bath and the molecular coupling to that bath. These results establish a multiscale mechanism by which condensed-phase environments can govern the connectivity and dynamics of an effective two-level system.
papers.authors: Nathan McLane, Richard C. Remsing, Leah G. Dodson

papers.title: Gibbsian Entropy for General Wigner Distributions
papers.abstract: We propose a definition of non-equilibrium Gibbsian entropy applicable to general quantum systems, computable from Wigner functions, for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states. We show that while the Wigner function is a quasi-probability distribution, fundamental results linking observables in repeated observations to the function, such as the law of large numbers, the central limit theorem and, crucially, the relation between the entropy and the cumulant generating function continue to apply. This ideas are the core of the large deviation theory, which allow to formulate a positive-definite definition of entropy based on our ignorance of the underlying state structure after repeated measurements of cumulants. This new definition is a parallel to the Gibbs entropy formulation, but it can also be used in out-of-equilibrium regimes. Some important properties of this entropy are discussed. In addition we derive some information theory quantities such as relative entropy, conditional entropy, mutual information and R\'enyi entropy. We then compare the results with Wehrl entropy for the 1D harmonic oscillator, for pure and mixed states. We conclude the the work discussing potential applications of this new formalism, ranging from quantum correlations beyond entanglement to thermalization in closed quantum systems.
papers.authors: Gabriel Rabelo-Soares, Yevgeniy Kovchegov, Giorgio Torrieri

papers.title: 99.9...% of the SU(2) BFSS ground state
papers.abstract: We solve for the ground-state wavefunction of the SU(2) BFSS matrix model by applying the Rayleigh-Ritz method to an auxiliary operator $H_{\mathrm{aux}}$.
